nodes.title: Auxiliary Siegel data for a Shimura datum
nodes.statement: Let (G, X) be a Shimura datum of Hodge type with reflex field E, p a prime, v | p a place of E and K = K_pK^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f) a neat compact open subgroup. An auxiliary Siegel datum for (G, X, K) at v is a finite nonempty family J of triples (ι_j, g_j, K_j)_{j∈J}, where ι_j : (G, X) → (GSp(V_j, ψ_j), S^±(V_j)) is an embedding of Shimura data into the Siegel datum of a symplectic ℚ-space, V_j(ℤ) ⊂ V_j is a lattice on which ψ_j is ℤ-valued and perfect at p (so its stabilizer K_{j,p} ⊂ GSp(V_j)(ℚ_p) is hyperspecial), K_j = K_{j,p}K_j^p is a neat compact open subgroup of GSp(V_j)(𝔸_f) and g_j ∈ G(𝔸_f) satisfies ι_j(g_jKg_j^{-1}) ⊂ K_j. Each triple induces a morphism of characteristic-zero Shimura varieties Sh_K(G, X) → Sh_{K_j}(GSp(V_j), S^±) ⊗_ℚ E, x ↦ ι_j(x g_j^{-1}), and J induces their product into ∏_j Sh_{K_j} ⊗ E. A singleton J = {(ι, 1, K‡)} with Sh_K → Sh_{K‡} a closed immersion is Madapusi Pera's choice; collections J of conjugations of one ι are Lan's and Boxer–Pilloni's.
hypotheses: (G, X) of Hodge type; K neat; the level K_j hyperspecial at p, that is the stabilizer of a lattice V_j(ℤ_p) self-dual for ψ_j.
No condition is imposed on K_p: the level of G at p is arbitrary; hyperspeciality is required only of the auxiliary Siegel levels.
proofSteps: Embeddings of Shimura data and the induced maps of Shimura varieties are those of ShimuraData D4 and ShimuraVarieties V1 (level maps and Hecke translations), composed with right translation by g_j.
If ψ_j is not perfect at p on a given lattice, replace V_j by Zarhin's space (V_j ⊕ V_j^∨)^4 with its perfect form (C7/zarhin-self-dual-replacement); this changes ι_j but not the generic fibre Sh_K.
The product of the induced maps is a morphism of E-schemes; its finiteness for suitable K_j is C7/generic-toroidal-finite-map.
acceptance: Every Hodge-type datum and neat level admits an auxiliary Siegel datum (Zarhin's replacement of any Hodge embedding).
The generic map of a singleton datum with K ⊂ K‡ small is a closed immersion Sh_K → Sh_{K‡} ⊗ E.

nodes.title: Zarhin's replacement and finiteness of the moduli map
nodes.statement: Let (V, ψ) be a symplectic ℚ-space with a lattice L on which ψ is ℤ-valued and nondegenerate. Then L′ = (L ⊕ L^∨)^4 carries a ℤ-valued perfect alternating form ψ′ whose restriction to the diagonal copy of L ⊕ L^∨ is ψ ⊕ ψ^∨ up to a fixed integral automorphism, and the map on moduli A ↦ (A ⊕ A^∨)^4 with Zarhin's principal polarization defines, for neat prime-to-p levels K^p ⊂ K′^p compatible with this embedding, a finite morphism of ℤ_(p)-stacks 𝒜_{g,d,K^p} → 𝒜_{8g,1,K′^p} extending the generic morphism of Siegel Shimura varieties; here 𝒜_{g,d} is the moduli stack of abelian schemes with a polarization of degree d² (any d, possibly divisible by p).
hypotheses: The level K′^p is chosen so that the induced map on level structures is defined; neatness is used only to work with algebraic spaces.
Finiteness is asserted over ℤ_(p); smoothness of 𝒜_{g,d} at p | d is not claimed.
proofSteps: Zarhin's trick: for an abelian scheme A with polarization λ, (A × A^∨)^4 carries a principal polarization built from λ and a quaternion of integers u with u ū = −1 modulo the degree (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.5, relative Zarhin's trick).

The map is quasi-finite: A is recovered up to finitely many choices as a direct factor of (A × A^∨)^4 with its induced polarization, by the finiteness of polarized automorphism groups (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6).

The map is proper by the valuative criterion: if (A × A^∨)^4 extends over a discrete valuation ring then so does A, since good reduction is inherited by isogeny factors (Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5); quasi-finite and proper gives finite.
acceptance: For g = 2, d = p the target is the principally polarized Siegel moduli of genus 16.
For d = 1 the map composes the identity of 𝒜_{g,1} with the closed immersion A ↦ (A × A^∨)^4.

nodes.title: Induced cone decompositions
nodes.statement: Let J be an auxiliary Siegel datum (C7/auxiliary-siegel-datum) and, for each j, Σ_j a K_j-admissible complete rational polyhedral cone decomposition for the Siegel datum of V_j. For each cusp label representative Φ of (G, X, K), with induced labels Φ_j = (ι_j, g_j)_*Φ, the induced decomposition Σ(Φ) of the closed cone of Φ is the set of nonempty intersections of the cone of Φ with preimages of products ∏_j σ_j, σ_j ∈ Σ_j(Φ_j), under the map of central lattices B_K(Φ) → ∏_j B_{K_j}(Φ_j). The family Σ = ι^*(Σ_j)_j is a K-admissible rational polyhedral cone decomposition, complete if each Σ_j is, possibly nonsmooth even when every Σ_j is smooth, and every admissible decomposition of (G, X, K) has a refinement that is induced from smooth projective Σ_j.
hypotheses: Cone conventions of ShimuraCompactifications C0: rational polyhedral, closed and salient, on the common lattice carrier; admissibility means compatibility under the arithmetic action with finitely many orbits.
Smoothness of Σ is not part of the construction.
proofSteps: Form Σ(Φ) by pulling back cones along the linear map of central lattices; faces and intersections pull back to faces and intersections, so Σ(Φ) is a fan on the cone of Φ (ShimuraCompactifications C0 common refinements).
Compatibility of Φ ↦ Φ_j with the arithmetic actions and with face maps of cusp labels gives admissibility; completeness pulls back because the cone of Φ maps into the cones of the Φ_j.
Given an admissible Σ′ of (G, X, K), refine the Σ_j so that each cone of Σ′ is a union of induced cones (Madapusi Pera 4.1.6 citing Harris; Lan16 §7).
acceptance: The induced decomposition of a complete admissible family is complete and admissible.
Induced cones of a smooth family can be nonsmooth for the induced lattice.

nodes.title: Finite maps of characteristic-zero toroidal compactifications
nodes.statement: With J and Σ = ι^*(Σ_j) as in C7/induced-cone-decomposition, the generic map of J extends to a morphism of E-schemes Sh^Σ_K → ∏_j Sh^{Σ_j}_{K_j} ⊗ E from Pink's toroidal compactification over E, it is finite, and it identifies Sh^Σ_K with the normalization of ∏_j Sh^{Σ_j}_{K_j} ⊗ E in Sh_K. On boundary charts it maps each boundary mixed Shimura variety Sh_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ) finitely to ∏_j Sh_{K_{Φ_j}}(Q_{Φ_j}, D_{Φ_j}) ⊗ E, compatibly with the torus-torsor and abelian-torsor towers, and each twisted torus embedding Sh_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) to the product of those for σ_j ⊇ σ.
hypotheses: Σ induced from complete K_j-admissible Σ_j; finiteness of the generic map Sh_K → ∏ Sh_{K_j} on the interior follows from the closed-immersion or level-change form of each ι_j.
proofSteps: Extend the map by the functoriality of toroidal compactifications for morphisms of data whose cone maps send cones into cones (ShimuraCompactifications C3, level and datum maps).

Finiteness: the map is proper (source proper) and quasi-finite, the latter checked stratum by stratum on boundary charts where it is a finite map of torus embeddings over finite maps of boundary bases (Harris, Lemma 3.1, as cited by Madapusi Pera 4.1.2).
Since Sh^Σ_K is normal (ShimuraCompactifications C2) and contains Sh_K densely, Zariski's main theorem identifies it with the normalization of the target in Sh_K.
acceptance: For a smooth Σ_1 on a Siegel datum and its own trivial auxiliary datum the map is the identity.
Over the boundary the map need not be a closed immersion even when Sh_K → Sh_{K‡} is.

nodes.title: The normalized toroidal model
nodes.statement: Let O be the localization O_{E,(v)} (or its completion O_{E_v}, or ℤ_p when E_v = ℚ_p), J an auxiliary Siegel datum and Σ = ι^*(Σ_j) induced from smooth complete projective Σ_j. Let 𝒜^{Σ_j}_{K_j} be the smooth proper integral toroidal compactification over ℤ_(p) of the Siegel moduli at the hyperspecial level K_j (ShimuraCompactifications C5). The normalized toroidal model 𝒮^Σ_K = 𝒮^Σ_K(J) is the normalization of ∏_j 𝒜^{Σ_j}_{K_j} ⊗ O in Sh^Σ_K along the finite map of C7/generic-toroidal-finite-map: the relative spectrum over the product of the integral closure of its structure sheaf in the pushforward of the structure sheaf of Sh^Σ_K. It is a normal algebraic space, proper and flat over O, with generic fibre Sh^Σ_K and a finite morphism to ∏_j 𝒜^{Σ_j}_{K_j} ⊗ O.
hypotheses: Σ_j smooth, complete and projective for the auxiliary Siegel models, so that 𝒜^{Σ_j}_{K_j} is a smooth projective scheme over ℤ_(p); Σ itself may be nonsmooth.
The construction uses only excellence and normality; no smoothness of the interior and no moduli interpretation at level K_p is asserted.
proofSteps: Normalize along the finite morphism Sh^Σ_K → ∏ 𝒜^{Σ_j}_{K_j} ⊗ E (Mathlib's relative normalization on schemes, glued on étale charts for algebraic spaces).
Finiteness of the normalization over the product: the product is of finite type over the excellent ring O, hence Nagata (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0).
Properness follows from finiteness over a proper base; flatness from torsion-freeness of the structure sheaf, which injects into its generic fibre; normality by construction.
acceptance: 𝒮^Σ_K is proper and flat over O with generic fibre Sh^Σ_K.
For the Siegel datum at hyperspecial level it is the Faltings–Chai compactification.

nodes.title: The interior of the normalized model
nodes.statement: The preimage 𝒮_K of ∏_j 𝒜_{K_j} ⊗ O under the finite map ν of C7/normalized-toroidal-model is an open dense subspace of 𝒮^Σ_K, it is the normalization of ∏_j 𝒜_{K_j} ⊗ O in Sh_K, it is normal, flat and of finite type over O with generic fibre Sh_K, and it does not depend on Σ. For a singleton J with Sh_K → Sh_{K‡} a closed immersion and K_p = K‡_p ∩ G(ℚ_p), 𝒮_K is the normalization of the Zariski closure of Sh_K in 𝒜_{K‡} ⊗ O (Kisin's integral model when K_p is hyperspecial and p > 2).
hypotheses: J auxiliary Siegel datum and Σ induced as in C7/normalized-toroidal-model.
proofSteps: Normalization commutes with restriction to open subspaces of the base, so the preimage of the open interior of the product is the normalization of that interior in the preimage of Sh_K, which is Sh_K because the generic toroidal map sends boundary to boundary.
Density: every irreducible component of 𝒮^Σ_K dominates O (flatness) and meets the generic fibre in a component of Sh^Σ_K, in which Sh_K is dense.
Independence of Σ: the interior normalization only involves the interiors of the auxiliary models.
For the closed-immersion case, the integral closure of the closure of Sh_K equals the integral closure in Sh_K by Zariski's main theorem.
acceptance: The interior of the normalized model of the modular curve at level K_0(p) is the normalization of the level-K^p curve in Y_0(p), not the Katz–Mazur moduli scheme a priori; ShimuraVarietiesPartII owns their comparison.

nodes.title: Transitivity and independence of auxiliary choices
nodes.statement: Let J and J′ be auxiliary Siegel data for (G, X, K) with induced decompositions Σ, Σ′. If there is a finite morphism ∏_{j∈J} 𝒜^{Σ_j}_{K_j} ⊗ O → ∏_{j′∈J′} 𝒜^{Σ′_{j′}}_{K′_{j′}} ⊗ O compatible with the generic maps from Sh^Σ_K (so that Σ = Σ′), then 𝒮^Σ_K(J) ≅ 𝒮^Σ_K(J′) canonically over the generic identification. In particular: the union J ⊔ J′ gives the same model as J whenever the projection of the product onto the J-factors is finite on the image; Zarhin's replacement of a self-dual factor and the direct-sum map from a product of principally polarized Siegel models to a single one do not change the model. In general 𝒮^Σ_K depends on J (Boxer–Pilloni Remark 3.4.21); for PEL data it depends only on the linear-algebraic collection of lattices, not on the auxiliary moduli chosen for them (Lan, Corollary 11.7).
hypotheses: Finite morphisms between the auxiliary products compatible with the generic maps; normality and excellence of all bases.
proofSteps: Integral closure is transitive: if A → B is finite then the integral closure of B in L equals the integral closure of A in L.
Apply locally on étale charts of the target product and glue by uniqueness of normalization.

For Zarhin's replacement and direct sums the morphisms of moduli are finite (C7/zarhin-self-dual-replacement; direct sum of principally polarized abelian schemes has finite fibres by uniqueness of decomposition up to finite ambiguity).
For PEL collections use the universal property of Lan16 Theorem 11.4, which does not involve the auxiliary choices (C8/pel-degenerating-families).
acceptance: Two auxiliary data related by a finite map of products give canonically isomorphic models; two data with no such map need not.

nodes.title: Normalized boundary towers and twisted torus embeddings
nodes.statement: For a cusp label representative Φ of (G, X, K) with induced labels Φ_j, let 𝒮_{K_{Φ_j}}(Q_{Φ_j}, D_{Φ_j}) → 𝒮_{K_{Φ_j}}(Q_{Φ_j}, D̄_{Φ_j}) → 𝒮_{K_{Φ_j},h}(G_{Φ_j,h}, D_{Φ_j,h}) be the integral boundary tower of the good Siegel model (torus torsor over an abelian scheme over a Siegel moduli space of smaller genus, ShimuraCompactifications C5). The normalized boundary tower 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ) → 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D̄_Φ) → 𝒮_{K_Φ,h}(G_{Φ,h}, D_{Φ,h}) is the normalization of the product of these towers in the characteristic-zero tower of Φ (ShimuraCompactifications C1–C2). For a cone σ of Σ(Φ) and σ_j with σ = ∩ preimages, 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) is the normalization of ∏_j 𝒮_{K_{Φ_j}}(Q_{Φ_j}, D_{Φ_j}, σ_j) in Sh_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ); it does not depend on the σ_j, its generic fibre is the twisted toric variety Sh_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ), and the normalization 𝒵_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) of the closed stratum of the product in the closed stratum Z_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) carries a finite map to it extending the closed immersion of generic fibres.
hypotheses: Φ a cusp label representative; Σ induced from smooth projective Σ_j.
proofSteps: Normalize each level of the product tower in the corresponding generic level; the maps of the tower are induced by the universal property of normalization.

Independence of σ_j: two choices differ by refinement of the auxiliary cones meeting the same relative interior; the normalizations of the corresponding torus embeddings agree on the open orbit and are finite over each other (Harris, Lemma 3.1, via Madapusi Pera 4.1.2).
Generic fibre: normalization commutes with flat base change to E, and Harris's lemma identifies the generic normalization with the twisted toric variety.
acceptance: Generic fibres of the normalized tower are the characteristic-zero boundary tower of ShimuraCompactifications C1–C2.
The normalized twisted torus embedding does not depend on the auxiliary cones σ_j inducing σ.

nodes.title: Normalized strata of the toroidal model
nodes.statement: For a cone label Υ = [(Φ, σ)] of (G, X, K, Σ) with image Υ_j in each auxiliary model, let 𝒵_K(Υ) be the normalization of ∏_j 𝒵_{K_j}(Υ_j) (the strata of the good Siegel models) in the characteristic-zero stratum Z_K(Υ) of Sh^Σ_K. There is a canonical isomorphism 𝒵_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) ≅ 𝒵_K(Υ) extending the generic one, and the map 𝒵_K(Υ) → ∏ 𝒵_{K_j}(Υ_j) ↪ ∏ 𝒜^{Σ_j}_{K_j} lifts to a map 𝒵_K(Υ) → 𝒮^Σ_K extending the locally closed immersion Z_K(Υ) ↪ Sh^Σ_K.
hypotheses: Σ induced; the generic identification Z_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) ≅ Z_K(Υ) uses that the group Δ°_K(Φ) is trivial (Madapusi Pera 4.1.4, using Cartan involutions and 2.1.20).
proofSteps: Construct both sides as normalizations of the same auxiliary objects in isomorphic generic fibres and apply uniqueness.
The lift exists by the universal property of the normalization 𝒮^Σ_K, since 𝒵_K(Υ) is normal and flat with generic fibre in Sh^Σ_K.
acceptance: The generic fibre of 𝒵_K(Υ) → 𝒮^Σ_K is the locally closed stratum of Sh^Σ_K.

nodes.title: Normalized models over the cyclotomic integers
nodes.statement: Let ℤ_p^cycl := ℤ_p[ζ_{p^∞}] = ⋃_m ℤ_p[ζ_{p^m}] (the noncompleted union) and ℚ_p^cycl its fraction field. For J and Σ as in C7/normalized-toroidal-model with O = ℤ_p (E_v = ℚ_p, or after base change), 𝒮^Σ_{K,ℤ_p^cycl} is the normalization of ∏_j 𝒜^{Σ_j}_{K_j} ⊗ ℤ_p^cycl in Sh^Σ_K ⊗ ℚ_p^cycl. It is the inverse limit (union of rings on affines) of the normalizations 𝒮^Σ_{K,ℤ_p[ζ_{p^m}]}; it is normal and flat over ℤ_p^cycl and not noetherian; its interior is the analogous normalization of the interiors; and the natural map to 𝒮^Σ_K ⊗_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p^cycl is integral and an isomorphism over the generic fibre, but in general not an isomorphism.
hypotheses: ℤ_p^cycl denotes the union ℤ_p[ζ_{p^∞}], not its p-adic completion; the p-adically completed variant is the p-adic completion of this model.
No noetherian hypothesis is available, so finiteness is proved at each finite level m and passed to the limit.
proofSteps: At each m, ℤ_p[ζ_{p^m}] is a complete discrete valuation ring and C7/normalized-toroidal-model applies with O = ℤ_p[ζ_{p^m}].

Integral closure commutes with filtered unions of the coefficient rings: an element integral over ⋃ R_m is integral over some R_m, so the normalization over ℤ_p^cycl is the colimit of rings of the normalizations at finite level on affine charts.
Normality and flatness pass to filtered colimits with flat transition maps; ℤ_p^cycl is a valuation ring whose value group is not discrete, hence it is not noetherian.
Non-isomorphism with base change: already for the modular curve at level Γ_1(p), the base change of the normalization over ℤ_p to ℤ_p[ζ_p] is not normal.
acceptance: The ℤ_p^cycl model is the union of the models over ℤ_p[ζ_{p^m}].
Its map to the base change of the ℤ_p model is an isomorphism after inverting p but not in general.

nodes.title: PEL data with a collection of lattices
nodes.statement: Fix an integral PEL datum (O, ⋆, L, ⟨·,·⟩, h_0) with reflex field F_0 satisfying Lan's condition 1.4.3.10, a prime p (with no unramifiedness assumption), and an open compact H ⊂ G(Ẑ) whose image in G(Ẑ^p) is neat. A lattice collection is a finite family {(g_j, L_j, ⟨·,·⟩_j)}_{j∈J}, where g_j ∈ G(𝔸_f), L_j ⊂ L ⊗ ℚ is an O-lattice with a pairing ⟨·,·⟩_j that is a rational multiple of ⟨·,·⟩ and integral on L_j, stable under g_jHg_j^{-1}. Each j defines a PEL moduli problem M_{H_j} isomorphic to M_H in characteristic zero (by g_j-translated quasi-isogeny), and for each j an auxiliary good-reduction moduli problem M_{H_j,aux} over O_{F_{0,j,aux},(p)} obtained by Zarhin's trick when ⟨·,·⟩_j is not prime to p, by restricting the O-action to a subalgebra unramified at p, and by keeping only the level away from p. The collection J determines the morphism M_H → ∏_{j∈J} M_{H_j,aux} ⊗ ℚ.
hypotheses: Lan's condition 1.4.3.10 on the integral PEL datum (achievable by modifying the integral data).
H^p neat; no hypothesis on the level at p, on ramification of O at p or on the residue characteristic.
proofSteps: Define each M_{H_j} as Lan's moduli problem for the j-th lattice; the characteristic-zero isomorphism M_H ≅ M_{H_j} is the quasi-isogeny twist of Lan16 §3.
Construct the auxiliary problems and the morphisms (4.13)–(4.15) as in Lan16 §4: Zarhin's trick (C7/zarhin-self-dual-replacement), restriction of the endomorphism structure, and level away from p.
acceptance: Every PEL datum and level with neat prime-to-p part admits a lattice collection with auxiliary good moduli.
For the singleton good-prime collection the auxiliary moduli problem is M_H itself.

nodes.title: Normalized interior and minimal models
nodes.statement: For a lattice collection J (C8/pel-lattice-collection), let M⃗_H be the normalization of ∏_{j∈J} M_{H_j,aux} in M_H, and M⃗^min_H the normalization of ∏_{j∈J} M^min_{H_j,aux} in M_H, where M^min_{H_j,aux} are the good-reduction minimal compactifications. Then: M⃗_H is a normal algebraic stack, flat over S⃗_0 = Spec O_{F_0,(p)}, with generic fibre M_H and a finite morphism to ∏ M_{H_j,aux}; for each j the tautological object over M_H extends to a polarized abelian scheme with O-structure (A⃗_j, λ⃗_j, i⃗_j) over M⃗_H satisfying the determinant condition, with level structure only over M_H; ω_{M_H} extends to ω_{M⃗_H, j} = ∧^top Lie^∨ A⃗_j. M⃗^min_H is a normal projective flat scheme over S⃗_0 containing M⃗_H as an open dense subscheme, with a finite morphism to ∏ M^min_{H_j,aux}, on which the line bundle ω_{M⃗^min_H, J}, the pullback of the external tensor product of ω^{⊗a_{j,0}}, is ample and restricts to ω^{⊗a_J}_{M_H} with a_J = Σ_j a_j.
hypotheses: As in C8/pel-lattice-collection; a_{j,0}, a_j ≥ 1 are the integers of Lan16 Lemma 5.30 making the auxiliary Hodge powers descend and be ample.
proofSteps: Normalize the product of auxiliary interiors and of auxiliary minimal compactifications in M_H (finite over excellent bases, hence finite).

Extend each tautological abelian scheme: the auxiliary one pulled back from M_{H_j,aux} is determined by A_j via Lan16 Lemma 4.1 (Zarhin), and the O-structure extends uniquely over the noetherian normal base by extension of homomorphisms (ShimuraCompactifications C4).
Ampleness: the pullback of an ample line bundle under a finite morphism is ample; projectivity and normality of M⃗^min_H follow; its restriction to M_H is ω^{a_J} by Lan16 Lemma 5.30.
acceptance: M⃗^min_H is normal, projective and flat over S⃗_0 with ample ω_J.
At a good prime with the singleton collection it is the good-prime minimal compactification.

nodes.title: Normalized toroidal models and their contraction
nodes.statement: Let Σ_j be compatible smooth projective admissible cone decompositions for the auxiliary problems and Σ the induced (possibly nonsmooth) decomposition for M_H. The normalization M⃗^tor_{H,Σ} of ∏_j M^tor_{H_j,aux,Σ_j} in M_H is a scheme proper and flat over S⃗_0 with a finite morphism to the auxiliary product; M⃗_H is the dense open preimage of the auxiliary interiors; the auxiliary contractions induce a proper morphism ∮⃗_H : M⃗^tor_{H,Σ} → M⃗^min_H, and M⃗^min_H ≅ Proj(⊕_{k≥0} Γ(M⃗^tor_{H,Σ}, ω^{⊗k}_{J})) compatibly with ∮⃗_H.
hypotheses: Σ_j smooth projective with Lan's condition 6.2.5.25; Σ induced by pulling back products of cones (C7/induced-cone-decomposition).
proofSteps: Proper flatness from finiteness over the proper smooth auxiliary product and torsion-freeness; the open dense interior by Zariski's main theorem.
The contraction is induced from the auxiliary contractions by the universal property of normalization.
The Proj comparison: the pullback of ω_J is ample over M⃗_H, the Proj maps finitely to M⃗^min_H and is an isomorphism over M⃗_H, so it is an isomorphism by normality (Zariski's main theorem).
acceptance: For the singleton good-prime collection and smooth Σ this is the good-prime toroidal model (Lan16 Corollary 11.8).

sources.match: Defines the normalized toroidal model from the product of auxiliary toroidal compactifications, proves it proper flat with dense interior, and identifies the normalized minimal model with the Proj of the sections of powers of the pulled-back Hodge line.

nodes.title: Putative boundary charts by normalization
nodes.statement: For a cusp label representative (Z_H, Φ_H, δ_H) of M_H, inducing auxiliary representatives for each j, define by normalization of the corresponding auxiliary boundary objects in the characteristic-zero ones: the normalized boundary moduli M⃗^{Z_H}_H (with degenerating families of the boundary abelian parts), the normalized abelian-scheme torsor C⃗_{Φ_H,δ_H} → M⃗^{Z_H}_H (proper), the E_{Φ_H}-torsor Ξ⃗_{Φ_H,δ_H} → C⃗_{Φ_H,δ_H} for the split torus E_{Φ_H} with character group S_{Φ_H}, and for each σ ∈ Σ_{Φ_H} the affine torus embedding Ξ⃗_{Φ_H,δ_H}(σ) with its σ-stratum Ξ⃗_{Φ_H,δ_H,σ}, the preimage of the auxiliary strata. If σ is smooth, Ξ⃗(σ) → C⃗ is smooth and surjective, Ξ⃗_σ is an E_{Φ_H,σ}-torsor over C⃗, smooth over C⃗ and hence flat over S⃗_0 when C⃗ is.
hypotheses: Same setting as C8/pel-normalized-toroidal; σ ⊂ P^+_{Φ_H}.
proofSteps: Normalize the auxiliary boundary moduli in the characteristic-zero boundary moduli (Lan16 Proposition 7.4), then the auxiliary abelian torsors and torus torsors (Propositions 8.1, 8.4, 8.7).

The torus E_{Φ_H} acts on the normalization because it acts compatibly on the auxiliary torsors and on the generic fibre; Proposition 8.14 shows that for smooth σ the normalized torus embedding is the relative torus embedding of a torsor, by comparing with the auxiliary embeddings along the finite map of tori.
Lemma 8.20 identifies the σ-stratum with the preimage of the auxiliary strata.
acceptance: For smooth σ, Ξ⃗(σ) is smooth over C⃗ and its σ-stratum is a torsor.
At a good prime the charts are those of Lan's book.

sources.match: Constructs the normalized boundary moduli, abelian torsors, torus torsors and torus embeddings by normalization, proves the torsor and smoothness statements for smooth cones, and identifies the closed strata.

nodes.title: Strata and formal completions of normalized PEL models
nodes.statement: In the setting of C8/pel-normalized-toroidal: (1) M⃗^tor_{H,Σ} is stratified by locally closed subschemes Z⃗[(Φ_H, δ_H, σ)] indexed by equivalence classes with σ ⊂ P^+_{Φ_H}, σ ∈ Σ_{Φ_H}, each open and closed in the preimage of the corresponding auxiliary stratum, with Z⃗[τ′] in the closure of Z⃗[τ] if and only if τ is a face of τ′; (2) the formal completion of M⃗^tor_{H,Σ} along Z⃗[(Φ_H, δ_H, σ)] is canonically isomorphic to the quotient of X⃗_{Φ_H,δ_H,σ} by the stabilizer, compatibly with the auxiliary completions; (3) each stratum is isomorphic to Ξ⃗_{Φ_H,δ_H,σ}, an E_{Φ_H,σ}-torsor over C⃗_{Φ_H,δ_H}, hence flat over S⃗_0 and normal, proper over M⃗^{Z_H}_H when σ is top-dimensional; (4) M⃗_H ⊗ 𝔽_p is dense in M⃗^tor_{H,Σ} ⊗ 𝔽_p, and closure relations of strata hold fibrewise in characteristic p.
hypotheses: Same setting; strata use the reduced structure.
proofSteps: Strata: compare with the auxiliary strata through the finite map (7.8) and the universal property (Lan16 Lemmas 9.3–9.12, Theorem 9.13).

Completions: the canonical map from the putative chart completion to the completion of M⃗^tor is finite, and both sides are excellent normal and flat with isomorphic rational fibres after refining to a common smooth refinement (Lan16 (10.1)–(10.14)); Zariski's main theorem gives Theorem 10.13.

Corollary 10.15 reads off the strata; density of the interior special fibre (Corollary 10.18) follows from flatness of the strata and the description of completions; Corollary 11.9 gives fibrewise closure relations.
acceptance: No irreducible component of M⃗^tor_{H,Σ} ⊗ 𝔽_p lies in the boundary.
For the singleton good-prime collection and smooth Σ the stratification is that of Lan's book (Lan16 Corollary 11.8).

sources.locator: Theorem 9.13, p. 51; Theorem 10.13, pp. 53–54; Corollaries 10.15 and 10.18, pp. 54–55; Corollary 11.9, p. 57
sources.match: Proves the stratification of the normalized toroidal model with its incidence relation, the isomorphism of formal completions with the putative charts, the torsor description and flatness of the strata, and density of the interior in the special fibre.

nodes.title: Degenerating families and the universal property
nodes.statement: (1) For each j ∈ J the polarized abelian scheme (A⃗_j, λ⃗_j, i⃗_j) over M⃗_H extends to a degenerating family (G⃗_j, λ⃗_j, i⃗_j, α⃗_{H_j}) of type M_{H_j} over M⃗^tor_{H,Σ} (a semi-abelian scheme with polarization and O-structure, abelian over M⃗_H), whose pullback to each completed chart X⃗_{Φ_H,δ_H,σ} is the Mumford family. (2) Universal property: if S is an irreducible noetherian normal S⃗_0-scheme with generic point η, η → M_H, and for each j a degenerating family of type M_{H_j} over S inducing η → M_{H_j}, then η → M_H extends (uniquely) to S → M⃗^tor_{H,Σ} if and only if at each geometric point of S the degeneration data lie in a cone of Σ (Lan16 Theorem 7.14's condition). (3) Consequently M⃗^tor_{H,Σ} depends only on the lattice collection, not on the auxiliary choices.
hypotheses: Same setting; level structures of the extended families are defined only over M_H.
proofSteps: Write M⃗^tor as an increasing union of opens U_i with U_0 = M⃗_H, each U_{i+1} ∖ U_i a closed stratum; extend the family across each stratum using the Mumford family on its completed chart and fpqc descent (Lan16 Lemma 11.1).
For (2), the degenerating families of type M_{H_j} determine auxiliary families over S by Lan16 Proposition 5.24, unique by extension of homomorphisms over normal bases, and Theorem 7.14 applies.
(3) is Lan16 Corollary 11.7: the universal property of (2) involves no auxiliary data.
acceptance: For the Siegel collection of Boxer–Pilloni §3.4.19 this gives semi-abelian G over A^tor_{g,d} extending the universal abelian scheme, with G^∨ and λ from the j-family (C13/siegel-bad-level-toroidal).

sources.locator: Lemma 11.1, Theorem 11.2, Theorem 11.4 and Corollary 11.7, pp. 55–57; Theorem 7.14, p. 38
sources.match: Extends the tautological families over the normalized toroidal model, proves the universal property for degenerating families over noetherian normal bases, and deduces independence of auxiliary choices.

nodes.title: Strata of normalized minimal models
nodes.statement: M⃗^min_H is stratified by locally closed subschemes Z⃗[(Φ_H, δ_H)] indexed by cusp labels, each canonically isomorphic to the normalized boundary moduli M⃗^{Z_H}_H; the contraction ∮⃗_H maps the toroidal stratum Z⃗[(Φ_H, δ_H, σ)] onto Z⃗[(Φ_H, δ_H)], and this surjection is the composite of Z⃗[(Φ_H, δ_H, σ)] ≅ Ξ⃗_{Φ_H,δ_H,σ} → M⃗^{Z_H}_H with the stratum isomorphism; it is proper when σ is top-dimensional. The fibres of ∮⃗_H are geometrically connected.
hypotheses: Same setting.
proofSteps: Strata of M⃗^min_H are defined via the auxiliary minimal strata and the finite map (6.6) (Lan16 Theorem 12.1).
Geometric connectedness of fibres of ∮⃗_H: Stein factorization and normality (Lan16 Lemma 12.9).
Identification of the strata with M⃗^{Z_H}_H by comparing formal completions of strict local rings (Lan16 Proposition 12.14, Theorem 12.16).
acceptance: For the modular curve the strata of M⃗^min_H are the interior and the finite flat cusps.

sources.locator: Theorem 12.1, p. 58; Lemma 12.9 and Proposition 12.14, pp. 60–61; Theorem 12.16, p. 62
sources.match: Stratifies the normalized minimal model by cusp labels with strata isomorphic to the normalized boundary moduli, and describes the contraction on strata.

nodes.title: Level changes and Hecke twists of normalized PEL models
nodes.statement: (1) For H ⊂ H′ and a subcollection J′ ⊂ J satisfying the conditions for H′, there are canonical morphisms M⃗_{H,J} → M⃗_{H′,J′}, M⃗^min_{H,J} → M⃗^min_{H′,J′} and, for compatible Σ, Σ′, M⃗^tor_{H,Σ,J} → M⃗^tor_{H′,Σ′,J′}, extending the characteristic-zero maps and mapping strata to strata. (2) Hecke twists by g ∈ G(𝔸_f^p) act compatibly. (3) These morphisms are proper but need not be finite, even on the interior: for a lattice-chain collection mapping to a singleton subcollection the map can contract curves (Lan16 Remark 13.10 and Example 13.12).
hypotheses: Same setting; compatibility of Σ and Σ′ means each cone of Σ maps into a cone of Σ′.
proofSteps: Induce the morphisms from projections of the auxiliary products onto the J′-factors and the universal property of normalization (Lan16 Proposition 13.1).
Toroidal and minimal versions as in Lan16 Propositions 13.4–13.9; Hecke twists by changing g_j (Lan16 Example 13.14, Propositions 13.15–13.19).
The non-finiteness example is Lan16 Example 13.12.
acceptance: The Klingen-to-spherical and Klingen-to-paramodular maps of Pilloni are instances with J′ ⊂ J (C14/klingen-projections).

sources.locator: Propositions 13.1, 13.4, 13.7, 13.9, Remark 13.10, Examples 13.11–13.14, Propositions 13.15 and 13.19, pp. 62–68
sources.match: Constructs the functorial morphisms for level change and subcollections, the Hecke twists, and shows by example that lattice-chain-to-singleton maps can be nonfinite.

nodes.title: Local properties pass from the interior to the boundary
nodes.statement: Let P be one of: reduced, geometrically reduced, normal, geometrically normal, Cohen–Macaulay, (R_0), geometric (R_0), (R_1), geometric (R_1), (S_i) for some i. A fibre of M⃗^tor_{H,Σ} → S⃗_0 has P if and only if the corresponding fibre of M⃗_H does. If Σ is smooth, P may also be regular, geometrically regular, (R_i) or geometric (R_i); in particular M⃗_H is regular if and only if M⃗^tor_{H,Σ} is. If Σ is smooth and M⃗_H is a local complete intersection over S⃗_0 then so is M⃗^tor_{H,Σ}.
hypotheses: Same setting; the last two assertions require Σ smooth.
proofSteps: By Lan16 Theorems 9.13 and 10.13 every complete local ring of M⃗^tor at a point s of a stratum Z⃗[(Φ_H, δ_H, σ)] is a complete local ring of Ξ⃗(σ) at a point of Ξ⃗_σ; the points of Spec of this ring off the boundary lie over points of M⃗_H, and every point of Ξ⃗ generizes a point of Ξ⃗_σ.

Hence a property P of excellent local rings that ascends and descends along flat local maps with geometrically regular fibres (completion, smooth morphisms; EGA IV₂ 6.5.3 and 7.8.3) passes from M⃗_H to Ξ⃗, from Ξ⃗ to C⃗ along the smooth surjection Ξ⃗ → C⃗, and back up to Ξ⃗(σ) and to M⃗^tor when Ξ⃗(σ) → C⃗ is smooth (σ smooth); this is Lan16 Propositions 14.1–14.2.

The lci assertion is not stated by Lan16; it follows by the same argument, since for a flat local homomorphism with regular closed fibre the source is a complete intersection if and only if the target is (Avramov's theorem on flat maps of complete intersections), and the lci locus is detected on completions.
acceptance: For the paramodular singleton and smooth Σ the toroidal model is lci over ℤ_p because the interior is (C14/normal-lci).

sources.match: Proves that regularity (for smooth Σ) and the listed fibre properties hold for the normalized toroidal model exactly when they hold for the normalized interior.
Deduces normality and the lci property of the Klingen and paramodular toroidal models from the local charts, the interior lci property and the boundary modular curves.

nodes.title: Minimal-model input for normalized blow-ups
nodes.statement: For a lattice collection J and the normalized minimal model M⃗^min_{H,J} of C8/pel-normalized-minimal, the hypotheses on M̃^min_{H,J} in ShimuraCompactifications C5.31 (Lan17 Theorem 6.1: a normal projective flat model over S̃_0 of the minimal compactification, with open normalized interior carrying the J-indexed tautological families) are satisfied by M⃗^min_{H,J}. Consequently, for every compatible projective cone decomposition Σ with polarization function pol (individual cones not necessarily smooth), Lan's normalized blow-up toroidal model M⃗^tor_{H,Σ,J} exists at every prime p with H^p neat, with formal torus-torsor charts and J-indexed families; when Σ is induced from smooth projective auxiliary decompositions it is canonically isomorphic to the normalized toroidal model of C8/pel-normalized-toroidal.
hypotheses: H^p neat; Σ projective and satisfying Lan's condition 6.2.5.25.
proofSteps: Normality, projectivity and flatness of M⃗^min_{H,J}, its open interior and its families are C8/pel-normalized-minimal and C8/pel-normalized-toroidal.
Apply ShimuraCompactifications C5.31 with this input.

For induced Σ, both models are normal, proper over M⃗^min_{H,J}, contain M⃗_H densely and have the same completed charts over a common smooth refinement (Lan17 §§4–5 compare with Lan16 §8); Zariski's main theorem identifies them.
acceptance: For Pilloni's Klingen and paramodular data this gives X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ} and X_{par,K,Σ} for good projective Σ (Pilloni Theorem 6.1.5.1, a special case of Lan17 Theorem 6.1).

sources.match: Constructs normalized blow-ups of the normalized minimal compactifications of Lan16 for all projective cone decompositions and compares them with the normalization models of Lan16 §7 through the putative boundary charts.
Supplies the normal projective flat minimal model and its interior families used as input.

nodes.title: Realizations of 1-motives
nodes.statement: Let S be a scheme and Q = [Y → G] a 1-motive over S: Y étale locally isomorphic to ℤ^r, G a semi-abelian scheme, extension of an abelian scheme B = Q^ab by a torus T with character group Q^mult (so Q^ét = Y), and a homomorphism Y → G. Its realizations are: the Tate modules T_ℓ(Q) = lim_n Q[ℓ^n] and T̂(Q), where Q[n] is the finite flat group scheme of n-torsion of the 1-motive (extension of Y/nY by G[n] built from Y → G); the de Rham realization H_dR(Q), the Lie algebra of the universal vector extension of the dual 1-motive, a locally free module of rank 2 dim B + rank Y + rank T with its weight filtration W_{−2} = Lie T ⊂ W_{−1} ⊂ W_0 = H_dR(Q) (graded pieces Lie T, H_dR(B), Y ⊗ O) and Hodge filtration F^0; over ℂ the Betti realization H_B(Q) with the mixed Hodge structure of weights −2, −1, 0. All realizations are compatible with tensor constructions, duality Q ↦ Q^∨ and base change, with the comparison isomorphisms between Betti, de Rham and étale realizations over ℂ, and over a degenerating chart V with the identification A[n] ≅ Q[n] of the Mumford construction.
hypotheses: S arbitrary for the étale and de Rham realizations (with n invertible on S for the étale ones); the Betti realization and its mixed Hodge structure only over ℂ.
Homological conventions: realizations are covariant in Q, as in Madapusi Pera §1.1.
proofSteps: Define Q[n] via the multiplication-by-n on the complex [Y → G] (Deligne, Hodge III 10.1); T̂ is its limit.
Define H_dR(Q) through the universal vector extension of Q^∨ (Deligne, Hodge III 10.1.7), with weight filtration from the extension structure and Hodge filtration from the vector extension.
Over ℂ, the Betti realization is H_1 of the analytic 1-motive with its mixed Hodge structure (Deligne, Hodge III 10.1.3); the comparison isomorphisms are those of loc. cit.
Over a degenerating chart, the Mumford construction (ShimuraCompactifications C4) identifies A[n] with Q[n] over V.
acceptance: For an abelian scheme the realizations are those of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4.
The weight-graded pieces of H_dR(Q) are Lie T, H_dR(B) and Y ⊗ O.

sources.match: Recalls 1-motifs over a base, their étale, de Rham, Betti and crystalline realizations with weight and Hodge filtrations, duality, and compatibility with the degeneration construction.
Recalls the equivalence between degenerating abelian schemes and degeneration data (Mumford, Faltings–Chai) through which the realizations of A and Q are compared.

nodes.title: Absolute Hodge tensors on boundary 1-motives
nodes.statement: Let (G, X) ↪ (GSp(H), S^±(H)) be a Hodge embedding with tensors {s_α} ⊂ H^⊗ whose pointwise stabilizer is G, and Φ a cusp label representative with induced Siegel label Φ‡. Over Sh_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ)(ℂ) the boundary 1-motive Q(Φ) pulled back from the Siegel boundary carries tensors s_{α,Φ,B}, s_{α,Φ,dR} and s_{α,Φ,ét} in W_0 of its realizations, identified with each other by the comparison isomorphisms; s_{α,Φ,dR} lies in F^0 ∩ W_0 and is horizontal. Then s_{α,Φ,dR} descends to a section of H_dR(Φ)^⊗ over the canonical model Sh_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ) over E, and s_{α,Φ,ét} to a section of H_{𝔸_f}(Φ)^⊗ over it.
hypotheses: (G, X) of Hodge type; K neat; the boundary mixed Shimura variety with its canonical model over E (ShimuraCompactifications C1–C2).
proofSteps: The tensors come from the mixed Hodge structure of the boundary (ShimuraCompactifications C1, boundary weight and Hodge filtrations).

Brylinski's theorem: Hodge classes on 1-motives over ℂ are absolutely Hodge, reducing to Deligne's theorem for abelian varieties (AutomorphicBundles B1/absolute-hodge-propagation) through the weight filtration.

Descent to the canonical model over E as in Kisin's argument for abelian schemes: an absolute Hodge class on a family over a variety defined over E, Galois-invariant at one fibre, is defined over E (Madapusi Pera 3.1.2 following Kisin 2.2).
acceptance: For Φ = (G, X^+, 1) the statement is Kisin's descent of the tensors on the universal abelian scheme over Sh_K.

nodes.title: Tensors of the 1-motive and of the abelian scheme agree
nodes.statement: Let Υ = [(Φ, σ)], t a point of the closed stratum Z_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ), R(Φ, σ, t) the complete local ring of Sh_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) at t and V = Spec R(Φ, σ, t) minus the boundary. Through the identification of R(Φ, σ, t) with a complete local ring of Sh^Σ_K, V carries both the boundary 1-motive Q and the abelian scheme A, with canonical isomorphisms T̂(Q) ≅ T̂(A) and H_dR(Q) ≅ H_dR(A) (Mumford's construction). These isomorphisms carry s_{α,Φ,ét} to s_{α,ét} and s_{α,Φ,dR} to s_{α,dR} for every α.
hypotheses: Characteristic zero; t may be taken ℂ-valued.
proofSteps: Over ℂ, identify the algebraic Mumford isomorphism T̂(Q) ≅ T̂(A) with the analytic one coming from the uniformization of the boundary neighbourhood (Madapusi Pera 2.2.13, compatibility of Mumford's construction with realizations).
For the analytic isomorphism the tensors correspond by construction, both being induced from the s_α ∈ H^⊗; argue identically for de Rham realizations.

The identifications hold for every α simultaneously.

nodes.title: The log Dieudonné crystal of a degenerating abelian scheme
nodes.statement: Let S = Spec R with R a complete noetherian normal local ring, flat over W = W(k) for a perfect field k of characteristic p, U ⊂ S the complement of a divisor with normal crossings giving S its log structure, and A an object of DEG(S, U): a semi-abelian scheme over S, abelian over U, with its degeneration data (a 1-motive Q over the completion with period pairing τ). The log Dieudonné crystal D(A) is a log F-crystal on the log crystalline site of the special fibre (finite locally free, with Frobenius, a logarithmic connection, a Hodge filtration and a weight filtration) with W_0 D(A) ≅ Hom(Q^ét, 1), W_1 D(A) ≅ D(Q^sab), gr^W_2 D(A) ≅ 1(−1) ⊗ Q^{mult,C}, duality D(A^∨) ≅ D(A)^∨, and a horizontal isomorphism H^1_dR(A/U) ≅ D(A)(S)|_U respecting both filtrations. It is constructed from the degeneration data as the Baer sum of D(Q) and the extension given by τ, and on the good-reduction locus it is the Dieudonné crystal of the p-divisible group.
hypotheses: k perfect of characteristic p; R complete noetherian normal local and W-flat; the log structure is the one defined by the boundary divisor; A has semi-abelian reduction along the boundary with split torus part after étale localization.
proofSteps: Reduce, by the equivalence of degenerating abelian schemes with degeneration data (Madapusi Pera 1.2.2; ShimuraCompactifications C4), to constructing D on degeneration data.

For totally degenerate data (abelian part 0) given by a pairing τ : Y × X → 𝔾_m over U, write D explicitly as the extension of Hom(X, O) by O(−1) ⊗ Y with log connection d log τ and Frobenius induced by the p-power map (Madapusi Pera A.1.1–A.1.5).

In general take the Baer sum of D(Q^cl), the Dieudonné crystal of the 1-motive with good reduction, and the totally degenerate extension (A.1.8–A.1.10); check the weight, duality and de Rham comparison properties on each piece.
acceptance: For an abelian scheme with good reduction D(A) is the Dieudonné crystal.
For the Tate curve the residue of the log connection is nonzero.

sources.match: Constructs a functor from degenerating abelian schemes to log Dieudonné crystals with weight filtration, with the stated weight-graded identifications, duality and de Rham comparison.

nodes.title: Semistable comparison for abelian varieties with semi-abelian reduction
nodes.statement: Let K/K_0 be a finite totally ramified extension of K_0 = W(k)[1/p], π a uniformizer, and A an abelian variety over K with split semi-abelian reduction over O_K. Let M_0(A) be the evaluation of the log Dieudonné crystal (C9/log-dieudonne-crystal) at W with its log structure, a filtered (φ, N)-module after the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism β_HK,π : K ⊗_{K_0} M_0(A) ≅ H^1_dR(A/K). There is a canonical isomorphism β_st,A : B_st ⊗_{ℚ_p} H^1_ét(A_{K̄}, ℚ_p) ≅ B_st ⊗_{K_0} M_0(A), compatible with Gal(K̄/K), φ, N and, after B_st → B_dR (depending on π), with the Hodge filtration via β_HK,π. Consequently (Coleman–Iovita) A has good reduction if and only if T_p(A) is crystalline, if and only if the monodromy N_0(A) vanishes.
hypotheses: K a finite extension of K_0 with perfect residue field k; split semi-abelian reduction (achieved after a finite extension); the embedding K ⊗ B_st → B_dR fixed by the choice of π.
proofSteps: Write A via Raynaud uniformization as G/Y with G semi-abelian of good reduction and Y the period lattice (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.3); the Tate module is an extension of the realizations of the 1-motive.

Construct β_st as the descent of the crystalline comparison for the good-reduction 1-motive combined with the explicit comparison for the totally degenerate extension, whose period is log τ ∈ B_st (Madapusi Pera 1.4.6–1.4.10, generalizing Faltings's construction for good reduction).

Compatibility with N: N_0(A) is the residue at u = 0 of the log connection on the evaluation of D(A) at the Breuil–Kisin type thickening Spf O_K ↪ Spf S_π; it vanishes exactly when D(A) has no log poles, that is when A has good reduction.
When a proper semistable model exists, this comparison agrees with the general semistable comparison of CohomologyComparisons CP.4 (Hyodo–Kato and Tsuji).
acceptance: For the Tate curve E_q over K, N_0 ≠ 0 and T_p(E_q) is semistable non-crystalline.
For an abelian variety with good reduction β_st restricts to Faltings's crystalline comparison.

sources.match: Constructs the semistable comparison isomorphism for abelian varieties with semi-abelian reduction from the log Dieudonné crystal, compatible with Galois action, Frobenius, monodromy and filtrations.

nodes.title: The canonical φ-module at a boundary point
nodes.statement: Fix a Hodge embedding with self-dual auxiliary lattice, a Siegel cusp label representative Φ‡ with cone σ‡ (σ‡° ⊂ H(Φ‡)), a closed point s‡_0 of the closed stratum of the Siegel twisted torus embedding over F̄_p, R(σ‡, s‡_0) its complete local ring with V = Spec R minus the boundary, and Q(σ‡, s‡_0) the tautological degeneration. Let M(σ‡, s‡_0) = D(A(σ‡, s‡_0))(S(σ‡, s‡_0)) (C9/log-dieudonne-crystal) with Frobenius lift φ = φ^sab ⊗̂ φ_σ (p-power on characters). It is canonically the Baer sum of D(Q^cl), for the 1-motive of the chosen trivialization of the torus torsor, and the split extension of O(−1) ⊗ X by Hom(X, O). Its fibre M_0 at the Teichmüller point is a φ-module over K_0 = W(F̄_p)[1/p] with weight filtration W_•M_0, symplectic form ψ_0 with values in K_0(−1), independent of the choices in the equivalence class of (σ‡, s‡_0), with a canonical isomorphism K_0 ⊗ Lie W_{Φ‡} ≅ K_0(−1) ⊗ Lie U_wt, where U_wt is the centre of the unipotent radical of the parabolic of GSp(M_0, ψ_0) stabilizing W_•M_0. For each K_0-point x of the rigid generic fibre Û^{an,◦}(σ‡, s‡_0) of V, the monodromy N_x of β_st at the degenerating abelian variety A_x is an element of the cocharacter lattice B ⊂ Lie W_{Φ‡} = (Lie U_wt)(−1) lying in σ‡°.
hypotheses: Hodge embedding with self-dual Siegel lattice and hyperspecial K‡_p; s‡_0 an F̄_p-point; analytic spaces as in Madapusi Pera A.4.
proofSteps: Trivialize the torus torsor over R^sab (strictly henselian) and write R(σ‡, s‡_0) ≅ R^sab ⊗̂ B(σ‡, s′_0) (Madapusi Pera 3.2.3).
Compute D(A) as the Baer sum (3.2.7) from the explicit description of the totally degenerate log Dieudonné crystal (A.1.5).
Compare M at different (σ‡, s‡_0) in one equivalence class via the blow-ups of 3.2.4–3.2.6 to obtain M_0 and its structures (3.2.9–3.2.10).
The monodromy at x is the residue of the log connection, computed from the period pairing τ_x, whose valuation lies in σ‡° (3.2.14).
acceptance: For the Tate curve at a cusp, M_0 has rank 2 with slopes 0 and 1 and the monodromy of a point with Tate parameter q_x is v_p(q_x) times the nilpotent generator.
M_0 does not depend on the representative of the equivalence class of (σ‡, s‡_0).

nodes.title: Canonical crystalline tensors at the boundary
nodes.statement: In the setting of C9/canonical-log-f-crystal, for a Hodge-type datum (G, X) with tensors {s_α} and a point t_0 of 𝒮^Σ_K over s‡_0, for every α there is a canonical tensor s_{α,st,0} ∈ M_0^⊗ such that: φ_0(s_{α,st,0}) = s_{α,st,0}; N_y(s_{α,st,0}) = 0 for every K_0-point y of Û^{an,◦}_G(σ‡, t_0) (the rigid generic fibre of the complete local ring R_G(σ‡, t_0) of 𝒮^Σ_K at t_0, off the boundary); and for every y over a finite extension L/K_0 and uniformizer π of L, β_st,y^{-1}(1 ⊗ s_{α,st,0}) = s_{α,ét,y} and β_HK,y,π(1 ⊗ s_{α,st,0}) = s_{α,dR,y}. The pointwise stabilizer of {s_{α,st,0}} in GL(M_0) is isomorphic to G_{K_0}.
hypotheses: Same setting; y ranges over points of the rigid generic fibre of the boundary complete local ring not on the boundary divisor.
proofSteps: At each point y, the semistable comparison of C9/semistable-comparison-abelian carries the étale tensors s_{α,ét,y} (Galois-invariant, by C9/absolute-hodge-one-motives) into (B_st ⊗ M_0(A_y))^⊗, φ- and N-invariant and in F^0; the compatibility of de Rham and étale tensors at each y is HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T1/hodge-tensor-comparison applied fibrewise.
Show that the resulting tensor in M_0 does not depend on y by horizontality in the family over Û^{an,◦}_G (parallel transport for the log connection, Madapusi Pera 3.3.6–3.3.8).

The scheme of isomorphisms H^∨(ℚ_p) ⊗ B ≅ M_0 ⊗ B carrying s_α to s_{α,st,0} has a B_st-point, hence is a G-torsor over K_0; by Steinberg's theorem over K_0 = W(F̄_p)[1/p] (ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.1.1, steinberg-quasi-split) it has a K_0-point, so the stabilizer is G_{K_0} (Madapusi Pera 3.4.1).
acceptance: In the PEL case the canonical tensors are the crystalline realizations of the reductions of the endomorphisms and polarization (Madapusi Pera Remark 3.3.10).

sources.match: Constructs canonical φ-invariant, monodromy-annihilated tensors in M_0 matching the étale tensors under the semistable comparison and the de Rham tensors under Hyodo–Kato.
Uses Steinberg's theorem to identify the stabilizer of the canonical tensors with G_{K_0}.

nodes.title: Rationality of Hodge cycles at the boundary (crystalline form)
nodes.statement: In the setting of C9/canonical-tate-tensors, let U_wt,G = U_wt ∩ G_{K_0} and B_G = B ∩ (Lie U_wt,G)(−1), with B ⊂ (Lie U_wt)(−1) the cocharacter lattice of the Siegel boundary torus via (3.2.10.1). Then the inclusion induces an isomorphism K_0 ⊗_ℤ B_G ≅ (Lie U_wt,G)(−1); equivalently rank_ℤ B_G = d_wt := dim_{K_0} U_wt,G. Moreover dim R^sab_G ≤ d − d_wt + 1, where d = dim Sh_K and R^sab_G is the normalization in R_G(σ‡, t_0) of the image of the complete local ring of the Siegel abelian-torsor base.
hypotheses: Same setting; d = dim X.
proofSteps: The monodromy elements N_x of points x of Û^{an,◦}_G lie in B_G (they annihilate the canonical tensors, C9/canonical-tate-tensors), so rank B_G is at least the dimension of their span, and at most d_wt.

Bound from above (Lemma 3.5.7): the Hodge filtrations F^•_y via β_HK give an unramified map η from the rigid space of R^sab to a Grassmannian landing in U^sab_{G,[μ]}, which has dimension d − d_wt because U_{G,[μ]} → U^sab_{G,[μ]} is a U_wt,G-torsor (Lemmas 3.5.3, 3.5.5); hence dim R^sab_G ≤ d − d_wt + 1.

Bound from below (3.5.9): a closed subscheme of a completed torus embedding over R^sab_G of dimension d + 1 needs at least d − dim R^sab_G + 1 independent monodromy directions; combining gives rank B_G ≥ d_wt.
acceptance: For the Siegel datum itself, B_G = B and the statement is the rank count dim U_wt = rank B.
In the PEL case, B_G is the sublattice of B commuting with the O-action, by functoriality of p-adic uniformization.

sources.match: Proves that the monodromy lattice B_G spans the twisted Lie algebra of U_wt,G, by an upper bound on the dimension of the abelian-part base from the Hodge filtrations and a lower bound from completed torus embeddings.
Calls this a rationality property of Hodge cycles with respect to p-adic uniformization and notes the simple PEL proof.

nodes.title: Reduction of the boundary torus torsor at a boundary point
nodes.statement: In the setting of C9/crystalline-rationality, let E be the Siegel boundary torus with cocharacter lattice B, E_G ⊂ E the subtorus with cocharacter lattice B_G, Ξ the restriction of the Siegel torus torsor to Spec R^sab, and Ξ_G = Ξ/E_G (a torsor under E/E_G). The tautological section ι_G of Ξ_G over Spec R_G(σ‡, t_0)[a_σ^{-1}] (a_σ an equation of the boundary) is already defined over Spec R^sab_G and is independent of the choice of (σ‡, s‡_0, t_0) in its equivalence class. Hence Ξ|_{Spec R^sab_G} has a canonical reduction of structure group to an E_G-torsor Ξ_G(ι_G).
hypotheses: Same setting as C9/crystalline-rationality; R^sab_G is integrally closed in R_G(σ‡, t_0) by construction.
proofSteps: Equivalent formulation (Madapusi Pera 3.4.4(2)): for a trivialization ι^sab and all characters h of E/E_G, some power α(h)^m lies in (R^sab_G)^×.

Over the rigid generic fibre the canonical trivialization is defined because the monodromy of every point lies in B_G (C9/crystalline-rationality and C9/canonical-tate-tensors); its descent to R^sab_G follows from the rigid-analytic extension lemmas (Madapusi Pera A.4) and the integrality of α(h) on the generic fibre (Madapusi Pera §3.6).
Independence of the representative: compare through the blow-ups relating equivalent pairs (3.2.4–3.2.6).
acceptance: For the Siegel datum itself B_G = B, E_G = E and the reduction is the identity.
In the PEL case the reduction is the subtorus fixed by the O-action, constructed directly from the moduli description (Lan16 §8).

sources.match: Proves that the induced section of the quotient torsor is defined over the normalized abelian-part base, giving a canonical reduction of the Siegel boundary torus torsor to the torus of B_G; calls this the key result of the paper.

nodes.title: Local structure at the boundary
nodes.statement: In the setting of C10/torsor-reduction there are a torus E^⋄_G with an isogeny E^⋄_G → E_G and an E^⋄_G-torsor Ξ^⋄_G over R^sab_G inducing Ξ_G(ι_G), such that for every (σ̃‡, s̃‡_0, t̃_0) in the equivalence class of (σ‡, s‡_0, t_0) the finite map Spec R_G(σ̃‡, t̃_0) → Spec R(σ̃‡, s̃‡_0) → Ξ(σ̃‡) lifts canonically to Spec R_G(σ̃‡, t̃_0) → Ξ^⋄_G(σ̃_G), σ̃_G = σ̃‡ ∩ (B_G ⊗ ℝ), identifying Spf R_G(σ̃‡, t̃_0) with the completion of the twisted torus embedding Ξ^⋄_G(σ̃_G) at a point of its closed stratum.
hypotheses: Same setting; this is a statement about complete local rings of 𝒮^Σ_K at boundary points in the special fibre.
proofSteps: Use the closed immersion Sh_K → Sh_{K‡,⋄} at a deeper Siegel level K‡,⋄ with K = K‡,⋄ ∩ G(𝔸_f) (Madapusi Pera 3.7.2) to see R_G as the normalization of a quotient of a complete local ring of the deeper Siegel chart.
The section of Ξ^⋄/E^⋄_G is defined over R^sab_G by C10/torsor-reduction, giving the reduction Ξ^⋄_G and a lift of the map into the twisted torus embedding.

Dimension count dim Ξ^⋄_G ≤ (d − d_wt + 1) + d_wt = dim R_G (C9/crystalline-rationality) forces Spec R_G to map finitely and dominantly onto the completion of the normal scheme Ξ^⋄_G(σ̃_G) at a point; normality gives the isomorphism (Madapusi Pera 3.7.4).
acceptance: At a boundary point of the modular curve the complete local ring is W[[t]] with t^w = q, the completion of the line bundle of 𝔾_m at its zero section.
The dimension count dim Ξ^⋄_G = dim R_G holds at every boundary point.

sources.match: Identifies the complete local ring of 𝒮^Σ_K at a boundary point with the completion of a twisted torus embedding over the normalized abelian-part base, using the reduction of structure group and a dimension count.

nodes.title: The abelian part of the boundary tower
nodes.statement: Assume K_p = K‡(n)_p ∩ G(ℚ_p) for some n ≥ 1, where K‡(n) is the full level-n subgroup of the self-dual Siegel level. For every cusp label representative Φ of (G, X), the abelian scheme A_K(Φ) → Sh_{K_Φ,h}(G_{Φ,h}, D_{Φ,h}) extends to an abelian scheme 𝒜_K(Φ) → 𝒮_{K_Φ,h}(G_{Φ,h}, D_{Φ,h}) (namely the normalization of the pulled-back Siegel abelian scheme in A_K(Φ)), and the A_K(Φ)-torsor Sh_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D̄_Φ) → Sh_{K_Φ,h} extends to an 𝒜_K(Φ)-torsor structure on 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D̄_Φ) → 𝒮_{K_Φ,h}(G_{Φ,h}, D_{Φ,h}).
hypotheses: K_p = K‡(n)_p ∩ G(ℚ_p) for some n ≥ 1 (this includes the case K_p = K‡_p ∩ G(ℚ_p) with n = 1).
proofSteps: For n = 1, the map A_K(Φ) → A_{K‡}(Φ‡) is a prime-to-p isogeny onto an abelian subscheme with orthogonal complement A′, and A_K(Φ) × A′ → A_{K‡}(Φ‡) is an isogeny of abelian schemes; the normalization of an abelian scheme in an isogeny factor over a normal base is an abelian scheme (Madapusi Pera A.3.8, Proposition 4.2.2).
For n ≥ 2 use the deeper Siegel level K‡,⋄ with K‡,⋄_p = K‡(n)_p, where the Siegel abelian scheme is Hom((1/n)X, Q^ab), and take a fibre product of abelian schemes.

The torsor structure is checked étale locally: a generic section extends by the valuative criterion and Weil's extension theorem for maps into abelian schemes (Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud 4.4, Theorem 1), identifying the normalized tower with A_K(Φ)|_U (Corollary 4.2.3).
acceptance: For a Siegel datum at hyperspecial level the abelian scheme is the integral Siegel boundary abelian scheme of ShimuraCompactifications C5.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.1.5(1), p. 71; Proposition 4.2.2 and Corollary 4.2.3, pp. 74–75
sources.match: Extends the abelian scheme and torsor structure of the boundary tower to the normalized integral models under the level hypothesis at p.

nodes.title: The normalized boundary torus torsor
nodes.statement: For every cusp label representative Φ, 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ) is an E_K(Φ)-torsor over 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D̄_Φ), extending the torsor structure of the generic fibre, where E_K(Φ) is the split torus over ℤ with cocharacter group B_K(Φ) (the lattice of Φ at level K). Consequently, for every rational polyhedral cone σ ⊂ W_Φ(ℝ)(−1), 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) is the twisted torus embedding of this torsor and 𝒵_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) is its closed stratum. The torus provided by C10/local-structure at each boundary point is E_K(Φ): B^⋄_G = B_K(Φ).
hypotheses: (G, X) of Hodge type, auxiliary datum as in C7; no hypothesis on K_p.
proofSteps: The E-action on the generic torsor extends to Ξ by normality; the torsor property is checked over complete local rings of the base.
Over the complete local ring at a point of the base, C10/local-structure exhibits Ξ as an E^⋄_G-torsor; it remains to identify E^⋄_G with E_K(Φ), that is B^⋄_G = B_K(Φ) (Lemma 4.2.11).

Lemma 4.2.11: using a section of the étale torsor I(Υ, s_0) of tensor-preserving level structures (Lemma 4.2.7) and the compatibility of β_st with tensors, the isomorphism (3.2.10.1) restricts to K_0 ⊗ Lie W_Φ ≅ K_0(−1) ⊗ Lie U_wt,G, and intersecting with the level lattice gives B^⋄_G = B_K(Φ).
Without this, normalization of the closure of a subtorus torsor need not be a torsor (Madapusi Pera Remark 4.2.9; see C7/normalized-boundary-tower, test notTorsor).
acceptance: For FKW's parabolic (pure part zero-dimensional) this gives the torus torsor ξ_K → C_K over O_{E,(v)} (C11/fkw-good-reduction).

sources.locator: Theorem 4.1.5(4), p. 71; Lemma 4.2.7, Proposition 4.2.8, Remark 4.2.9 and Lemma 4.2.11, pp. 77–79
sources.match: Proves that the normalized boundary mixed Shimura model is a torsor under the expected torus, by identifying the torus of the local structure theorem with E_K(Φ) through the tensor-preserving level torsor.

nodes.title: Stratification of the normalized toroidal model
nodes.statement: For every cone label Υ ∈ Cusp^Σ_K(G, X), the map 𝒵_K(Υ) → 𝒮^Σ_K of C7/normalized-stratum-model is a locally closed immersion, and 𝒮^Σ_K = ⊔_Υ 𝒵_K(Υ) set-theoretically; the closure of 𝒵_K(Υ) is ⊔_{Υ′ ≼ Υ} 𝒵_K(Υ′). For every Siegel cone label Υ‡, the reduced preimage (𝒮^Σ_K ×_{𝒮^{Σ‡}} 𝒵_{K‡}(Υ‡))_red is normal and flat over ℤ_(p) and is the disjoint union of the 𝒵_K(Υ) with ι_*Υ = Υ‡. In particular every stratum is flat over O, the boundary contains no irreducible component of the special fibre, and every boundary point of the special fibre lifts to characteristic zero in the same stratum.
hypotheses: (G, X) of Hodge type; Σ induced; no hypothesis on K_p.
proofSteps: Flatness and normality of reduced preimages of Siegel strata: by C10/local-structure the completed ring of the preimage is R^sab_G ⊗̂ of the completed ring of a toric stratum of Ξ^⋄_G(σ_G), whose reduced closed stratum is a torus, smooth over ℤ (Proposition 4.2.4).

The finite birational map from ⊔_{ι_*Υ=Υ‡} 𝒵_K(Υ) to this normal flat scheme is an isomorphism (Corollary 4.2.5); the closure relation follows from the characteristic-zero relation and that of the Chai–Faltings compactification.
acceptance: No irreducible component of the special fibre of 𝒮^Σ_K lies in the boundary (used by Boxer–Pilloni, sourceIssues E67).
For the modular curve at level K_0(p) the strata are the interior and the cusps, each flat over ℤ_p.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.1.5(2),(3), p. 71; Proposition 4.2.4 and Corollary 4.2.5, pp. 75–77
sources.match: Stratifies 𝒮^Σ_K by the normalized strata with the expected closure relation and shows the reduced preimages of Siegel strata are normal and flat over ℤ_(p).

nodes.title: Formal completions along strata
nodes.statement: For Υ = [(Φ, σ)], the canonical isomorphism 𝒵_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) ≅ 𝒵_K(Υ) lifts to an isomorphism of formal algebraic spaces 𝒮̂_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) ≅ (𝒮^Σ_K)^∧_{𝒵_K(Υ)} between the completion of the twisted torus embedding along its closed stratum and the completion of 𝒮^Σ_K along the stratum, restricting on the generic fibre to Pink's isomorphism (ShimuraCompactifications C2) and compatible with the finite maps to the Siegel completions.
hypotheses: Same setting.
proofSteps: Both formal spaces are finite over the Siegel completion (𝒮^{Σ‡}_{K‡})^∧ ≅ 𝒮̂_{K‡_{Φ‡}}(…, σ‡); by the extension lemma for finite normal formal algebras (Madapusi Pera A.3.2) it suffices to compare complete local rings at points of the special fibre as algebras over the Siegel complete local ring.
These agree by the proof of C10/boundary-torus-torsor and C10/local-structure (Proposition 4.2.13).
acceptance: Over the generic fibre the isomorphism is Pink's description of the completion along a boundary stratum.
For the Siegel datum at hyperspecial level it is the formal completion statement of ShimuraCompactifications C5.4.

sources.match: Identifies the completion of 𝒮^Σ_K along a stratum with the completion of the normalized twisted torus embedding along its closed stratum.

nodes.title: Toroidal compactifications of Hodge type (Madapusi Pera, Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: For (G, X) of Hodge type, any neat K (arbitrary at p), an auxiliary Siegel datum and an induced complete admissible Σ: 𝒮^Σ_K is a proper normal flat algebraic space over O_{E,(v)} containing 𝒮_K as an open dense subspace whose complement is a relative effective Cartier divisor over O_{E,(v)}; it carries the stratification of C10/stratification with completions described by C10/formal-completion; every point has an étale neighbourhood V such that V|_{𝒮_K} ↪ V is étale over 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ) ↪ 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ) for some Φ, σ. After replacing Σ by a smooth refinement (with its normalized model), every complete local ring of 𝒮^Σ_K at a geometric point of the stratum of (Φ, σ) is isomorphic to a power series ring over a complete local ring of the abelian-torsor base 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D̄_Φ) (and over one of 𝒮_{K_Φ,h}(G_{Φ,h}, D_{Φ,h}) under the level hypothesis of C10/abelian-torsor-extension), hence to a complete local ring of 𝒮_K: the singularities of the compactification are no worse than those of the interior. Consequently étale-local properties (smoothness, reducedness, Cohen–Macaulayness, local complete intersection) of 𝒮_K and of the boundary pure models pass to 𝒮^Σ_K.
hypotheses: Hodge type; neat level; Σ induced and complete; the refinement statement uses the refined normalized model of C10/refinements.
proofSteps: Combine C10/formal-completion with Artin approximation (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.6) to obtain the étale neighbourhood comparison.
The complement of the open torsor in a twisted torus embedding is a relative Cartier divisor; transport this through the étale comparison and the stratification.

For a smooth refinement both the torsor and its torus embedding are smooth over the abelian-torsor base 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D̄_Φ); since 𝒮_K is étale locally isomorphic to the torsor near the boundary, every complete local ring of the base times a power series ring occurs as a complete local ring of 𝒮_K. Under the level hypothesis of C10/abelian-torsor-extension the base is an abelian-scheme torsor over 𝒮_{K_Φ,h}.
acceptance: For K_p arbitrary the theorem is agnostic to the special fibre of 𝒮_K: it holds where G is ramified at p.
For the modular curve at level K_0(p) the boundary is the finite flat cusp divisor and the singularities at cusps are smooth points.

sources.locator: Theorem 1, p. 3, and its proof, p. 72
sources.match: States and proves that the normalized model is a compactification with relative Cartier boundary, the expected stratification and completions, and singularities no worse than those of the interior after refinement.

nodes.title: Refinements and independence of the Siegel decomposition
nodes.statement: (1) 𝒮^Σ_K does not depend on the choice of Σ‡ with ι^*Σ‡ = Σ. (2) For an admissible refinement Σ′ of Σ there is a normal integral model 𝒮_K ↪ 𝒮^{Σ′}_K over O_{E,(v)} with a proper birational map 𝒮^{Σ′}_K → 𝒮^Σ_K extending Sh^{Σ′}_K → Sh^Σ_K and stratifications satisfying the conclusions of C10/main-theorem; the auxiliary datum can be chosen so that Σ′ is induced. (3) For the refinement map f : 𝒮^{Σ′}_K → 𝒮^Σ_K, f_*O = O and R^if_*O = 0 for i > 0.
hypotheses: Same setting; Σ′ admissible refining Σ.
proofSteps: (1) from C10/formal-completion and the extension lemma A.3.4: the completions along strata do not involve Σ‡.

(2) by the toroidal-embedding methods of Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat Ch. II applied to the étale-local charts, or by choosing the Siegel decomposition so that Σ′ is induced (Harris, as cited in Remark 4.1.6).

(3) étale locally f is a toric refinement of twisted torus embeddings over the normal base, so ShimuraCompactifications C3 (universal toric structure-sheaf acyclicity) applies (Madapusi Pera 5.1.3(2), following Faltings–Chai V.1.2(b)).
acceptance: For the blow-up of a smooth two-dimensional cone the refinement map has f_*O = O and no higher direct images.
Two Siegel decompositions inducing the same Σ give canonically isomorphic models.

sources.locator: Remark 4.1.6, p. 72; proof of Proposition 5.1.3(2), p. 83
sources.match: Shows independence of Σ‡, constructs models for refinements with the same stratification properties, and deduces the vanishing of higher direct images of the structure sheaf from the étale-local structure.

nodes.title: Embeddings of Shimura data and Hecke correspondences
nodes.statement: Let η : (G′, X′) ↪ (G, X) be an embedding of Hodge-type data, K′ ⊂ G′(𝔸_f) neat, g ∈ G(𝔸_f) with gη(K′)g^{-1} ⊂ K, and Σ′ admissible for (G′, X′, K′) refining (η, g)^*Σ, with Σ complete. Then the finite map 𝒮_{K′} → O_{E′,(v′)} ⊗ 𝒮_K extends uniquely to (η, g) : 𝒮^{Σ′}_{K′} → O_{E′,(v′)} ⊗ 𝒮^Σ_K, carrying 𝒵_{K′}(Υ′) into 𝒵_K((η, g)_*Υ′) and inducing on formal completions the maps of boundary charts (4.1.12.2). In particular prime-to-p Hecke correspondences (η = id, g ∈ G(𝔸_f^p)) extend to toroidal models for compatible pairs of cone decompositions; they do not act on a single fixed Σ in general.
hypotheses: Hodge type; the place v′ of E′ lies over v; Σ complete; compatibility of cone decompositions is part of the hypothesis.
proofSteps: On boundary charts the map (4.1.12.1) of normalized boundary towers is finite and extends to the twisted torus embeddings for cones with η(σ′) ⊂ σ meeting σ°.
Glue by the characteristic-zero map of ShimuraCompactifications C3 and the extension lemma for normal formal completions (Madapusi Pera 2.1.29 and A.3.4).
acceptance: Over a one-dimensional cusp of a GSpin variety the cone decomposition is forced, so prime-to-p Hecke correspondences extend uniquely over the preimage of the complement of the zero-dimensional cusps (C15/gspin-one-dimensional-cusps).

sources.match: Extends maps of integral models for embeddings of Shimura data and Hecke translations to toroidal models for compatible cone decompositions, compatibly with strata and formal completions.

nodes.title: Properness of the interior
nodes.statement: 𝒮_K is proper (equivalently projective) over O_{E,(v)} if and only if G^ad is ℚ-anisotropic, if and only if G^ad(ℚ) contains no nontrivial unipotent element.
hypotheses: Hodge type; neat K.
proofSteps: If G^ad has a proper ℚ-parabolic, the boundary of 𝒮^Σ_K is a nonempty relative Cartier divisor flat over O (C10/stratification), so 𝒮_K is not proper.
If not, Σ is empty, 𝒮^Σ_K = 𝒮_K is proper (and projective by C12/minimal-compactification).
acceptance: Shimura curves attached to indefinite quaternion algebras over ℚ give proper integral models; modular curves do not.

sources.match: Characterizes properness of the integral model by anisotropy of G^ad, read off from the stratification.

nodes.title: Potential good reduction when the Mumford–Tate group is anisotropic (Morita)
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field F whose Mumford–Tate group MT_A is anisotropic modulo its centre. Then A has potentially good reduction at every finite place of F.
hypotheses: F a number field; MT_A is independent of the complex embedding (Deligne).
proofSteps: By Zarhin's trick replace A by an abelian variety isogenous to A^8 with a principal polarization.
(MT_A, X_A) ↪ (GSp(H), S^±(H)) is an embedding of Shimura data of Hodge type; with K = K‡ ∩ G(𝔸_f) the integral model 𝒮_K is proper over O_{E,(v)} by C10/projectivity-criterion.
A arises from an F′-point of 𝒮_K for a finite F′/F; by properness it extends over O_{F′,(v′)}, so A has good reduction at v′.
acceptance: An abelian variety with CM by a field (Mumford–Tate group a torus, hence anisotropic modulo centre) has potentially good reduction everywhere.
An elliptic curve with non-integral j-invariant has Mumford–Tate group GL_2, which is isotropic, so the theorem does not apply.

sources.locator: Theorem 5, p. 6; Theorem 4.1.9 and its proof, pp. 72–73
sources.match: Deduces Morita's conjecture from the properness criterion for integral models of Hodge type.

nodes.title: Connected components of the integral model
nodes.statement: If the special fibre k(v) ⊗ 𝒮_K is geometrically reduced, then for every finite F/E and place w | v the natural maps π_0(F ⊗_E Sh_K) ← π_0(O_{F,(w)} ⊗ 𝒮_K) → π_0(k(w) ⊗ 𝒮_K) are bijections.
hypotheses: Hodge type; geometric reducedness of the special fibre of the interior is a hypothesis.
proofSteps: By C10/main-theorem the special fibre of 𝒮^Σ_K is geometrically reduced, and 𝒮_K is fibrewise dense in it.
For a flat proper algebraic space with geometrically reduced special fibre, Stein factorization reduces to a finite étale O_{E,(v)}-scheme, where the bijections are clear.
acceptance: For the modular curve with neat level the special fibre is geometrically reduced and the three sets of components are the components of the cyclotomic field of the level.
The hypothesis of geometric reducedness cannot be dropped: for the level K_1(p^2) model the special fibre is nonreduced.

sources.match: Compares connected components of generic, integral and special fibres when the special fibre is geometrically reduced.

nodes.title: Rationality of Hodge cycles under p-adic uniformization (étale form)
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field F with totally degenerate reduction at a place v (a torus with character group X_g = ℤ^g), Raynaud uniformization 1 → X_g → Hom(X_g, 𝔾_m)^an → A^an_{F_v} → 1, and for each prime ℓ let U_ℓ ⊂ GL(V_ℓ(A)) be the unipotent radical stabilizing the induced extension 0 → X_g ⊗ ℚ_ℓ(1) → V_ℓ(A) → Hom(X_g, ℚ_ℓ) → 0, so Lie U_ℓ = ℚ_ℓ(1) ⊗ Hom(X_g^∨, X_g). Let G = MT_A. Then B_G := Hom(X_g^∨, X_g) ∩ (Lie G_{ℚ_ℓ})(−1) is independent of ℓ, and ℚ_ℓ(1) ⊗ B_G ≅ Lie U_ℓ ∩ Lie G_{ℚ_ℓ} for every ℓ.
hypotheses: Totally degenerate reduction at v; the image of G_{ℚ_ℓ} in GL(V_ℓ(A)) is determined up to inner automorphism.
proofSteps: Realize A as a point of the Hodge-type Shimura variety of (MT_A, X_A) near a zero-dimensional cusp of the Siegel boundary.

The torus torsor of C10/boundary-torus-torsor has cocharacter lattice B_K(Φ) = B_G at the corresponding point; the non-emptiness of the torsor I(Υ, s_0) of tensor-preserving level structures identifies 𝔸_f(1) ⊗ Lie W_Φ with Lie U_{G,𝔸_f} (Remark 4.2.12).
acceptance: For a product of Tate curves E_{q_1} × E_{q_2} with multiplicatively independent q_i the Mumford–Tate group is GL_2 ×_{G_m} GL_2 and B_G has rank 2.
B_G does not depend on ℓ.

sources.match: States the ℓ-independent rationality of Hodge cycles with respect to p-adic uniformization and deduces it from the flatness of the boundary and the tensor-preserving level torsor.

nodes.title: p-integral Hodge embeddings
nodes.statement: A p-integral Hodge embedding of (G, X) is a Hodge embedding ι : (G, X) ↪ (GSp(H), S^±(H)) together with a reductive model G_{ℤ_(p)} of G over ℤ_(p), a ℤ-lattice H(ℤ) on which ψ is perfect, and a closed immersion of ℤ_(p)-groups G_{ℤ_(p)} ↪ GL(H_{ℤ_(p)}) extending ι, such that K_p = G_{ℤ_(p)}(ℤ_p) (hyperspecial) and K‡_p is the stabilizer of H(ℤ_p); in addition one fixes tensors {s_α} ⊂ H(ℤ_(p))^⊗ whose pointwise stabilizer in GL(H_{ℤ_(p)}) is G_{ℤ_(p)}.
hypotheses: G admits a reductive model over ℤ_(p); such lattices and tensors always exist (Kisin 2.3.1, 1.3.2; Kim–Madapusi Pera for p = 2).
proofSteps: Choose a G_{ℤ_(p)}-stable lattice (Kisin, Lemma 2.3.1) and, by Zarhin's trick, a self-dual one (C7/zarhin-self-dual-replacement).
A reductive closed subgroup of GL(H_{ℤ_(p)}) is the pointwise stabilizer of finitely many tensors (Kisin, Proposition 1.3.2).
acceptance: Every Hodge-type datum with G unramified at p admits a p-integral embedding after Zarhin's replacement.
The tensors cut out exactly G_{ℤ_(p)} inside GL(H_{ℤ_(p)}).

sources.match: Defines p-integral symplectic embeddings and arranges integral tensors cutting out the reductive model, citing Kisin.

uses.how: the hyperspecial hypothesis under which the compactification is smooth and canonical
the GSpin lattice self-dual at p gives a p-integral embedding via Kuga–Satake

nodes.title: Smooth toroidal compactifications at hyperspecial level (Madapusi Pera, Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: Assume ι is p-integral (C11/p-integral-embedding), p > 2 or the hypotheses of Kim–Madapusi Pera at p = 2, so that 𝒮_K is smooth over O_{E,(v)} (Kisin). Then: the boundary pure models 𝒮_{K_Φ,h}(G_{Φ,h}, D_{Φ,h}) are smooth, the parabolic P_Φ extends to a parabolic of G_{ℤ_(p)} and G_{Φ,h} has a reductive model with hyperspecial level; the boundary towers 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ) → 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D̄_Φ) → 𝒮_{K_Φ,h} are a torus torsor over an abelian-scheme torsor over a smooth base; for smooth complete Σ, 𝒮^Σ_K is smooth over O_{E,(v)} (projective when Σ is projective) with boundary a relative normal crossings divisor; and 𝒮^Σ_K with its stratification depends only on Σ, not on the p-integral embedding.
hypotheses: p-integral embedding at hyperspecial level; Kisin's smoothness theorem for 𝒮_K and for the boundary data (recorded as a gap owned by ShimuraVarietiesPartII).
proofSteps: Boundary data: P_Φ extends by properness of the scheme of parabolics; Q_Φ extends with reductive image in the Levi (Madapusi Pera 4.3.4, citing Pink 1.6.9), so K_{Φ,h,p} is hyperspecial and Kisin's theorem applies to 𝒮_{K_Φ,h}.
The tower is smooth over the base by C10/boundary-torus-torsor and C10/abelian-torsor-extension (here n = 1).
The immersion 𝒮_K ↪ 𝒮^Σ_K is étale locally 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ) ↪ 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ, σ), smooth with normal crossings boundary for smooth σ (C10/main-theorem).
Independence of the embedding: the boundary integral models are canonical (C11/canonical-boundary-models) and the completions along strata are determined by them (A.3.4).
acceptance: For a PEL datum at a good prime this recovers Lan's smooth compactification (ShimuraCompactifications C5).
For the modular curve with neat prime-to-p level the compactification is the smooth compactified modular curve over ℤ_(p).

sources.locator: Theorem 2, p. 4; §4.3.3–4.3.4 and proof of Theorem 2, pp. 80–81
sources.match: Proves smoothness and normal crossings of the toroidal compactification of Kisin's model at hyperspecial level, and independence of the symplectic embedding.
Uses that the canonical integral model of the GSpin Shimura variety has a smooth toroidal compactification whose boundary strata are flat divisors with formal completions of the expected shape.
