nodes.title: Canonical models of the boundary mixed Shimura varieties
nodes.statement: At hyperspecial level with a p-integral embedding, the projective limit 𝒮_p(Q_Φ, D_Φ) = lim_{K^p} 𝒮_{K_{Φ,h,p}K^p_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ) (finite étale transition maps) is a regular, formally smooth O_{E,(v)}-scheme locally of finite type with generic fibre Sh_p(Q_Φ, D_Φ), and it is a canonical model: for every regular formally smooth O_{E,(v)}-scheme S, every map E ⊗ S → Sh_p(Q_Φ, D_Φ) extends to S → 𝒮_p(Q_Φ, D_Φ). It and its Q_Φ(𝔸_f^p)-action depend only on (G, X) and G_{ℤ_(p)}.
hypotheses: p-integral embedding; Kisin's smoothness for the boundary pure data.
proofSteps: Smoothness from C11/smooth-toroidal (its boundary part) and the fact that the tower is étale locally isomorphic to 𝒮_K.
Extension property as in Kisin's proof of 2.3.8, replacing the extension theorems for abelian schemes by those for 1-motives (Madapusi Pera A.3.5, A.3.6).
acceptance: For the Siegel datum at hyperspecial level the canonical boundary models are the Faltings–Chai integral boundary moduli.
The extension property fails for non-formally-smooth S (for instance ℤ_p[√p]).

sources.match: Shows the prime-to-p limit of the normalized boundary mixed Shimura models is a canonical integral model with the extension property for regular formally smooth schemes.

nodes.title: The de Rham G-torsor over the compactification
nodes.statement: At hyperspecial level with a p-integral embedding and smooth complete Σ: (1) the first relative de Rham homology of the universal abelian scheme extends, with its Hodge filtration and an integrable connection with logarithmic poles along the boundary, to a filtered vector bundle H_dR(Σ) on 𝒮^Σ_K, characterized on completions along strata by the de Rham realization of the universal 1-motive (via the log Dieudonné crystal); (2) the de Rham tensors s_{α,dR} on 𝒮_K extend uniquely to sections s_{α,dR,Σ} ∈ H^0(𝒮^Σ_K, H_dR(Σ)^⊗); (3) the functor P^Σ_dR(ι) of trivializations O_T ⊗ H(ℤ_(p)) ≅ H_dR(Σ)|_T carrying s_α to s_{α,dR,Σ} is a G_{ℤ_(p)}-torsor extending P_dR(ι), and the sub-functor respecting the Hodge filtration is a canonical reduction to a P_μ-torsor over O_{F,(w)} ⊗ 𝒮^Σ_K for a model μ of the Hodge cocharacter; (4) for another p-integral embedding ι′ there are canonical isomorphisms P^Σ_dR(ι) ≅ P^Σ_dR(ι′) and P^Σ_dR,μ(ι) ≅ P^Σ_dR,μ(ι′).
hypotheses: p-integral embedding; smooth complete Σ; F/E finite with a place w | v over which μ is defined.
proofSteps: (1): evaluate the log Dieudonné crystal of the tautological 1-motive on boundary charts (C9/log-dieudonne-crystal), descend by faithfully flat descent and glue (Madapusi Pera 4.3.1); it agrees with the analytic canonical extension over ℂ.

(2)–(3): the complement U of the special fibre of the boundary has codimension 2 in the normal 𝒮^Σ_K, so vector bundles and their sections extend uniquely from U; over 𝒮_K this is Kisin's 2.3.9, and over the generic fibre near the boundary the tensors extend by the analytic description (Madapusi Pera 4.3.7, 4.3.9).
(4): compare both with the torsor of the direct-sum embedding; check over Sh_K(ℂ) (Proposition 4.3.10).
acceptance: For the Siegel datum the torsor is the frame bundle of H_dR(Σ) with its symplectic form, the canonical extension of AutomorphicBundles B3.

sources.match: Extends the de Rham bundle with log connection, the de Rham tensors and the G- and P_μ-torsors of tensor-preserving trivializations over the compactification, independently of the embedding.

planet.name: De Rham torsor over the compactification

nodes.title: Unramified good reduction of boundary torus torsors
nodes.statement: Let (G, X) be of Hodge type, G reductive over ℤ_p (K_p = G(ℤ_p) hyperspecial, p > 2 or p = 2 under Kim–Madapusi Pera), K = K_pK^p neat, P ⊂ G a ℚ-parabolic as in Farb–Kisin–Wolfson 3.3.11 with unipotent radical U and centre Z, ξ_K = U(ℤ)\U(ℝ)Z(ℂ) → C_K the torus bundle over the abelian scheme C_K, and Σ a fan in X_*(Z(ℂ)/Z(ℤ))_ℚ giving a smooth torus embedding ξ_K(Σ) with normal crossings boundary D_K(Σ). Then (ξ_K(Σ), D_K(Σ)) and ξ_K → C_K have unramified good reduction at p in the sense of Farb–Kisin–Wolfson 2.2.12: they extend to a smooth torus embedding with relative normal crossings boundary over a smooth abelian-scheme torsor over an absolutely unramified discrete valuation ring O_{E_v} (E_v/ℚ_p unramified), namely the normalized boundary tower and twisted torus embeddings of the corresponding cusp label.
hypotheses: Hyperspecial level; ξ_K and C_K identified with the analytifications of the boundary mixed Shimura varieties of Madapusi Pera §2.1.7, 2.1.13 (Pink 6.10).

Farb–Kisin–Wolfson 2.2.12 defines unramified good reduction for proper smooth pairs; for the nonproper pair (ξ_K(Σ), D_K(Σ)) the definition is used with properness omitted, as in their Theorem 3.3.17.
proofSteps: Identify ξ_K → C_K with the boundary tower Sh_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ) → Sh_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D̄_Φ) over a zero-dimensional pure base for the cusp label of P (FKW 3.3.11 citing Pink and Madapusi Pera 2.1).

By C11/smooth-toroidal the integral boundary tower is a torus torsor over an abelian-scheme torsor over a smooth (here finite étale) base, and the twisted torus embeddings for smooth σ are smooth with relative normal crossings boundary.
E_v is unramified over ℚ_p because G is unramified at p, so O_{E_v} is absolutely unramified; descend from O_{E,(v)} to O_{E_v} by completion.
acceptance: For FKW's parabolic the pure part is zero-dimensional, so C_K is an abelian scheme over a finite étale O_{E,(v)}-scheme.

nodes.title: Canonicity of the minimal compactification at hyperspecial level
nodes.statement: At hyperspecial level with a p-integral embedding, the minimal compactification 𝒮^min_K of C12/minimal-compactification and its stratification are, up to unique isomorphism, independent of the p-integral embedding; for every admissible Σ, cusp label Φ and σ ∈ Σ(Φ), the induced map 𝒵_K([(Φ, σ)]) → 𝒵_K([Φ]) is smooth.
hypotheses: Hyperspecial level; p-integral embeddings.
proofSteps: Compare the minimal models of two embeddings via the normalization of the image of the product map from the canonical toroidal model; both projections are isomorphisms on 𝒮_K ∪ Sh^min_K, whose complement has codimension ≥ 2.

Smoothness: the quotient map 𝒮_{K_Φ,h} → Δ^fin_K(Φ)\𝒮_{K_Φ,h} is étale because the map to the Siegel boundary model factors through it and is unramified (Kisin 2.3.9: complete local rings of 𝒮_{K_Φ,h} are quotients of Siegel ones).
acceptance: For the Siegel datum the minimal model is Faltings–Chai's integral minimal compactification and the stratum maps are smooth.
Two p-integral embeddings give the same minimal compactification up to unique isomorphism.

nodes.title: The Hodge line on the normalized toroidal model
nodes.statement: For an auxiliary Siegel datum and complete Σ, the Hodge line ω_K(Σ) on 𝒮^Σ_K is the pullback along ν of ω_{K‡}(Σ‡) = det(H_dR(Σ‡)/F^0H_dR(Σ‡))^{⊗−1} on the good Siegel model, equivalently det(Lie^∨) of the pulled-back universal semi-abelian scheme. On a boundary chart of a cusp label Φ it decomposes as ω_K(Φ) = ω^ét(Φ) ⊗_ℤ ω^ab_K(Φ), where ω^ab_K(Φ) is the Hodge line of the abelian scheme over 𝒮_{K_Φ,h} and ω^ét(Φ) = det(gr^W H^g(ℤ))^{⊗−1} is a free ℤ-module of rank one; in particular ω_K(Φ) is pulled back from 𝒮_{K_Φ,h}.
hypotheses: Σ complete; the decomposition uses the weight-graded pieces of the de Rham realization of the 1-motive (C9/one-motive-realizations).
proofSteps: Pull back along the finite map ν (C7/normalized-toroidal-model).
Independence of K‡ and Σ‡: two choices are dominated by a third through finite maps, and the Siegel Hodge lines pull back to each other.
On boundary charts take determinants of the weight-graded pieces of H_dR(Φ, σ) (Madapusi Pera (5.1.4.1)).
acceptance: ω_K(Σ) is ample on 𝒮_K up to the boundary contraction: its pushforward to the minimal compactification is ample.
For the modular curve ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω¹(log cusps).

sources.match: Defines the Hodge bundle on the Siegel compactification, restricts it to 𝒮^Σ_K, shows independence of choices and compatibility with refinements, and decomposes it on boundary charts.

nodes.title: Sections of the Hodge line
nodes.statement: (1) A positive power of ω_K(Σ) is generated by its global sections over 𝒮^Σ_K. (2) For a refinement Σ′ of Σ and n ≥ 0, H^0(𝒮^Σ_K, ω^{⊗n}) → H^0(𝒮^{Σ′}_K, ω^{⊗n}) is an isomorphism. (3) The graded O_{E,(v)}-algebra ⊕_n H^0(𝒮^Σ_K, ω^{⊗n}) is finitely generated.
hypotheses: Σ complete; O_{E,(v)} excellent.
proofSteps: (1) Moret-Bailly's theta-constant argument for semi-abelian families over normal excellent bases (ShimuraCompactifications C5.32, hodgeLine_generated), as in Faltings–Chai V.2.1.
(2) Projection formula with f_*O = O and R^if_*O = 0 (C10/refinements).
(3) From (1) and properness as in Lan's book 7.2.2.6.

Sections of ω^{⊗n} on 𝒮^Σ_K and on any refinement agree.

nodes.title: Fourier–Jacobi expansions on Hodge-type models
nodes.statement: For a cusp label representative Φ, write 𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ, D_Φ) = Spec_{𝒮_{K_Φ}(Q_Φ,D̄_Φ)} ⊕_{ℓ∈S_K(Φ)} Ψ(ℓ)_K(Φ), S_K(Φ) the character group of E_K(Φ) and Ψ(ℓ) line bundles, and set FJ(ℓ)_K(Φ) = π_*Ψ(ℓ)_K(Φ) on 𝒮_{K_Φ,h}. The Fourier–Jacobi expansion along Υ = [(Φ, σ)] is the map FJ_{(Φ,σ)} : H^0(𝒮^Σ_K, ω^{⊗n}) → ∏_{ℓ∈S_K(Φ)} H^0(𝒮_{K_Φ,h}, FJ(ℓ)_K(Φ) ⊗ ω^{⊗n}_K(Φ)) obtained by restricting to the completion along 𝒵_K(Υ) (C10/formal-completion) and expanding in the completed character decomposition. It does not depend on σ (write FJ_Φ), its image lies in the Δ_K(Φ)-invariants of the product over the submonoid P_K(Φ) of characters pairing nonnegatively with the cone H(Φ), and it is compatible with the isomorphisms ρ(γ, q) between equivalent cusp label representatives.
hypotheses: Σ complete; Δ_K(Φ) the arithmetic group of Φ acting through its action on characters and on 𝒮_{K_Φ,h}.
proofSteps: The completion (5.1.5.1) of the torsor along the σ-stratum is the completed sum over ℓ ∈ S_K(Φ, σ) of Ψ(ℓ); the projection formula along π gives the expansion.
Independence of σ and the positivity of the support: compare two cones through a common refinement and use the Koecher-type argument of Madapusi Pera 5.1.7–5.1.8.
Compatibility with ρ(γ, q): ρ(γ, q)^*Q(Φ′) ≅ Q(Φ) induces ρ(γ, q)^*ω_K(Φ′) ≅ ω_K(Φ) (5.1.6.1).
acceptance: For the modular curve the expansion is the q-expansion at the cusp.
Only characters pairing nonnegatively with the positivity cone occur.

nodes.title: The minimal compactification of Hodge type
nodes.statement: 𝒮^min_K := Proj(⊕_n H^0(𝒮^Σ_K, ω^{⊗n})) for complete Σ. It is a normal projective O_{E,(v)}-scheme independent of Σ, with a canonical surjective map ∮_{Σ′} : 𝒮^{Σ′}_K → 𝒮^min_K with geometrically connected fibres for every sufficiently fine complete Σ′ (the Stein factorization of the map given by a basepoint-free power of ω). It satisfies: (1) 𝒮_K → 𝒮^min_K is an open immersion with complement flat over O_{E,(v)}; (2) ω extends to an ample line bundle ω^min_K with ∮^*ω^min_K ≅ ω_K(Σ); (3) a stratification 𝒮^min_K = ⊔_{[Φ]} 𝒵_K([Φ]) by cusp classes, 𝒵_K([Φ]) = Δ^fin_K(Φ)\𝒮_{K_Φ,h}(G_{Φ,h}, D_{Φ,h}) mapping by a locally closed immersion, with closure relation given by the order on cusp classes; (4) compatibility with strata: ∮^{-1}(𝒵_K([Φ])) = ⊔_σ 𝒵_K([(Φ, σ)]); (5) if 𝒮^1_K ⊂ 𝒮^Σ_K is the preimage of the complement of the strata of codimension ≥ 2, then H^0(𝒮^Σ_K, ω^{⊗n}) ≅ H^0(𝒮^1_K, ω^{⊗n}), and if G^ad has no factor PGL_2 then H^0(𝒮^Σ_K, ω^{⊗n}) ≅ H^0(𝒮_K, ω^{⊗n}) (Koecher). Universal property: for a very ample L on T and f : 𝒮^{Σ′}_K → T with f^*L ≅ ω^{⊗N}, f factors uniquely through ∮_{Σ′}.
hypotheses: Hodge type; neat K arbitrary at p; Σ complete.
proofSteps: Projectivity and normality from finite generation and normality of 𝒮^Σ_K (C12/hodge-sections; Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud 6.7, Lemma 2).

The constant term of FJ_Φ shows the composite 𝒵_K(Φ, σ) → 𝒮^min_K factors through Δ^fin_K(Φ)\𝒮_{K_Φ,h} (5.2.3); images of distinct cusp classes are disjoint (5.2.7) using the stratification of 𝒮^Σ_K and the Siegel case.
Each 𝒵_K([Φ]) → 𝒮^min_K is unramified by C12/minimal-complete-local-rings, finite onto its image and birational (checked over ℂ, Pink 6.3), hence a locally closed immersion (5.2.9).
Ampleness of ∮_*ω as in Lan's book 7.2.4.1; flatness of the boundary from flatness of the strata (C10/stratification).
acceptance: For the Siegel threefold at hyperspecial level the minimal boundary consists of curves and points.
The boundary of 𝒮^min_K is flat over O_{E,(v)}.

nodes.title: Complete local rings of the minimal compactification
nodes.statement: Let x be a geometric point of 𝒮^min_K lifting to a point y of 𝒵_K([Φ]) ⊂ 𝒮_{K_Φ,h}. Then the completed local ring of 𝒮^min_K at x is canonically [∏_{ℓ∈P_K(Φ)} FJ(ℓ)_K(Φ)^∧_y]^{Δ_K(Φ)}, the invariants under Δ_K(Φ) of the product of completed stalks of the Fourier–Jacobi sheaves over characters pairing nonnegatively with H(Φ).
hypotheses: Same setting as C12/minimal-compactification.
proofSteps: As in Lan's book 7.2.3.13: compute the completion of 𝒮^min_K at x through the formal functions on the preimage of x in 𝒮^Σ_K (formal functions for proper maps, ShimuraCompactifications C3.6a) and the completed charts of C10/formal-completion, then take invariants of the arithmetic group.

In particular prime-to-p Hecke correspondences extend to 𝒮^min_K, without any compatibility condition on cone decompositions.
hypotheses: Same setting as C10/functoriality.
proofSteps: Apply the universal property of C12/minimal-compactification to the composite of the toroidal map of C10/functoriality with the contraction, for compatible cone decompositions; uniqueness makes the result independent of them.

nodes.title: Coordinates and the unipotent action at a zero-dimensional cusp
nodes.statement: Let ℓ ≠ p, K_n the level obtained from the Siegel full level-ℓ^n subgroup, and x_n a zero-dimensional cusp of 𝒮^min_{K_n} ⊗ k (k = F̄_p) with cusp label representative Φ: P_Φ is an admissible parabolic with unipotent radical U_P and centre W, B_{K_n} ⊂ W(ℚ) the level lattice with dual S_{K_n}, Δ_{K_n} its arithmetic group and H ⊂ W(ℝ) the open self-adjoint cone. Then the complete local ring of 𝒮^min_{K_n,k} at x_n is R_{ℓ^n} = k[[q^λ]]^{Δ_{K_n}}_{λ≥0} (λ ∈ S_{K_n} pairing nonnegatively with H), and on R_ℓ = ⋃_n R_{ℓ^n} the group 𝔹_ℓ = B_{K_n} ⊗ ℤ[1/ℓ] ⊂ W(ℚ_ℓ), which fixes the compatible system of cusps, acts by T(∑ a_λ q^λ) = ∑ e((T, λ)) a_λ q^λ, where e : ℤ[1/ℓ] → μ_{ℓ^∞}(k) is the character a/ℓ^n ↦ ζ_{ℓ^n}^a determined by the cusp and the level structure.
hypotheses: Hodge type, hyperspecial level at p, ℓ ≠ p; zero-dimensional cusp, so the pure part 𝒮_{K_Φ,h} is finite and the abelian part trivial.
proofSteps: Specialize C12/minimal-complete-local-rings: for a zero-dimensional cusp FJ(ℓ) are rank-one free modules over the finite base, giving the invariant power series ring.

The prime-to-p Hecke action of G(ℚ_ℓ) on lim_n 𝒮^min_{K_n,k} restricts to W(ℚ_ℓ) ∩ stabilizer = 𝔹_ℓ, acting on the torus coordinates q^λ by the characters e((T, λ)) (Chai 1995, p. 452, via Madapusi Pera 2.1.11–2.1.18).
acceptance: For the modular curve at ∞ and level ℓ^n, R_{ℓ^n} = k[[q^{1/ℓ^n}]] and T = a/ℓ^n acts by q^{1/ℓ^n} ↦ ζ_{ℓ^n}^a q^{1/ℓ^n}.

sources.match: Describes the complete local ring at a zero-dimensional cusp as invariant power series in the cusp coordinates and the action of B_ℓ by roots of unity, following Madapusi Pera 2.1.11–2.1.18 and Corollaries 5.1.8, 5.2.8 and Chai.
Supplies the Fourier–Jacobi description of the completed local rings.

nodes.title: Siegel moduli of polarization type δ
nodes.statement: For g ≥ 1 and d ≥ 1 let 𝒜_{g,d} be the stack over ℤ of abelian schemes of relative dimension g with a polarization of degree d² (PELModuli M6.4, de Jong). For δ = (δ_1 | δ_2 | ⋯ | δ_g) with ∏ δ_i = d, let M_δ = diag(δ_1, …, δ_g, 1, …, 1) ∈ GL_{2g}(ℚ), K_δ = M_δ GL_{2g}(Ẑ) M_δ^{-1} ∩ GSp_{2g}(𝔸_f), and 𝒜_{g,δ} ⊂ 𝒜_{g,d} the locally closed substack where the kernel of the polarization is étale locally isomorphic to ∏_i (ℤ/δ_i × μ_{δ_i}). Then 𝒜_{g,δ,ℚ} = S_{K_δ,ℚ} and 𝒜_{g,d,ℚ} = ⊔_δ S_{K_δ,ℚ}. With a neat prime-to-p level K^p, 𝒜_{g,d,K^p} is an algebraic space of finite type over ℤ_(p).
hypotheses: Any d, including p | d; smoothness over ℤ_(p) holds only for p ∤ d.
proofSteps: Define the type loci by the étale-local type of the finite flat kernel of the polarization; local constancy of the type on the generic fibre gives the decomposition.
Identify 𝒜_{g,δ,ℚ} with the Shimura variety of level K_δ through the lattice M_δℤ^{2g} with its induced form (PELModuli M5.2 in characteristic zero).
acceptance: 𝒜_{2,p,ℚ} = S_{K_{(1,p)},ℚ}, the paramodular Shimura variety.
For p ∤ d the type loci are open and closed in 𝒜_{g,d} ⊗ ℤ_(p).

nodes.title: Toroidal models of Siegel varieties at arbitrary level at p
nodes.statement: Let K = K_pK^p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(𝔸_f) with K^p neat and K_p arbitrary, and choose d_1, …, d_r, types δ_i and conjugation-inclusions K ↪ K_{δ_i}. Define A^tor_{g,d_i} over ℤ_p as the normalized toroidal model of 𝒜_{g,d_i,K^p} (C7/normalized-toroidal-model for its own Zarhin auxiliary datum, or C8/pel-normalized-toroidal for the singleton collection), and, for cone decompositions such that S^tor_{K,ℚ} → ∏_i A^tor_{g,d_i,ℚ} is finite, S^tor_K := the normalization of ∏_i A^tor_{g,d_i} × Spec ℤ_p in S^tor_{K,ℚ_p}. It is normal, proper and flat over ℤ_p with interior S_K (the normalization of ∏ 𝒜_{g,d_i,K^p}), equal to the normalized model of the auxiliary datum obtained by composing with Zarhin's replacement (C7/normalization-transitivity); it carries the stratification, completions and degenerating families of C8 and C10, and its variant over ℤ_p^cycl is C7/cyclotomic-normalized-model.
hypotheses: Finiteness of S^tor_{K,ℚ} → ∏ A^tor_{g,d_i,ℚ} for the chosen cone decompositions, supplied by C7/generic-toroidal-finite-map for induced decompositions.
proofSteps: A^tor_{g,d} exists as a normalized model, carrying the semi-abelian G extending the universal abelian scheme (C13/semiabelian-extension).
Normalization along the finite map from S^tor_{K,ℚ_p}; transitivity identifies the result with the normalization of the product of Zarhin good models, so C8 (collections) and C10 (Hodge type) apply.
Dependence on the auxiliary choices (Boxer–Pilloni Remark 3.4.21) is that of C7/normalization-transitivity; for PEL collections the model depends only on the lattices (Lan16 Corollary 11.7).
acceptance: For K_p = G(ℤ_p) the model is the good Siegel toroidal compactification.
For g = 1 and K_p = K_0(p) the model is the compactified X_0(p) over ℤ_p.

nodes.title: The semi-abelian scheme, its dual and polarization over A^tor_{g,d}
nodes.statement: Over the normalized toroidal model A^tor_{g,d} of 𝒜_{g,d,K^p} over ℤ_p (any d, including p | d) there are semi-abelian schemes G and G^∨ extending the universal abelian scheme and its dual, and a homomorphism λ : G → G^∨ extending the polarization; they are unique up to unique isomorphism, and over the generic fibre ∐_δ S^tor_{K_δ,ℚ_p} they are the universal semi-abelian schemes of the toroidal compactifications.
hypotheses: A^tor_{g,d} the normalized model; uniqueness over the normal noetherian base.
proofSteps: Existence of G: Lan16 Theorem 11.2 for the singleton collection of the degree-d² lattice (C8/pel-degenerating-families), whose degenerating family of type M_H is a semi-abelian scheme with polarization.

G^∨: apply the same theorem to the dual lattice, or take the semi-abelian extension of the dual abelian scheme; λ extends uniquely by extension of homomorphisms over normal bases (ShimuraCompactifications C4, hom_extend).
acceptance: Over the interior, λ : G → G^∨ is the given polarization of degree d².
For the Tate curve at a cusp of A^tor_{1,1}, G is the Tate curve and λ the principal polarization.

sources.match: Extends the tautological polarized abelian schemes of the collection to degenerating families over the normalized toroidal model.

nodes.title: The Iwahori-level normalized model and its isogeny chain
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and K_{p,n} ⊂ GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p) the Iwahori subgroup of level p^n (reduction mod p^n in the Borel). Over the generic fibre there is the self-dual chain of isogenies A = A_g → A_{g+1} → ⋯ → A_{2g} → A_1 → ⋯ → A_g = A with total map [p^n], where ker(A_g → A_{g+i}) is totally isotropic in A[p^n], étale locally (ℤ/p^n)^i, and A_{g+i} carries a polarization of degree d_i² with d_0 = 1 and d_i = p^{n(g−i)} (1 ≤ i ≤ g). Define S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} as the normalization of ∏_{i=0}^{g} A^tor_{g,d_i} × Spec ℤ_p in S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},ℚ_p} (C13/deep-level-toroidal-model). Over it, with A_{g+i} the pullback of G from the i-th factor and A_j (1 ≤ j ≤ g − 1) the pullback of G^∨ from the factor of A_{2g−j}, the chain extends uniquely to a chain of isogenies of semi-abelian schemes with total map [p^n].
hypotheses: n ≥ 1 (the chain is trivial for n = 0); the printed degrees are corrected as in sourceIssues E65: the polarization of A_{g+i} has degree d_i² = p^{2n(g−i)}.
proofSteps: Apply C13/deep-level-toroidal-model to the collection of the g + 1 polarization degrees.
Over the interior A_j ≅ A_{2g−j}^∨ for 1 ≤ j ≤ g − 1, which justifies the choice of G^∨-factors.

Each isogeny of the chain extends uniquely over the normal base (ShimuraCompactifications C4, hom_extend; Faltings–Chai I.2.7), and the identity for the composite holds because it holds on a dense open.
acceptance: The composite of the extended chain is [p^n] on all of S^tor.
For g = 1, n = 1 the model is the compactified X_0(p) with E → E/H → E.

nodes.title: Graded pieces of the Iwahori chain are quasi-finite flat
nodes.statement: For 1 ≤ i ≤ 2g let Gr_i be the kernel, over all of S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}, of the map of the extended chain whose target is A_i. Over the interior Gr_i = H_i/H_{i−1} in the flag ordering g + 1, …, 2g, 1, …, g (with 0 before H_{g+1}), a finite flat group scheme of order p^n with Gr_{2g−i+1} ≅ Gr_i^D. Over S^tor, each Gr_i is quasi-finite and flat, but in general not finite at the boundary: its order can drop on boundary strata.
hypotheses: Same setting; the indexing follows sourceIssues E66.
proofSteps: Each map of the chain is an extended isogeny of p-power degree over a normal base, hence quasi-finite flat (ShimuraCompactifications C4.11, isogeny_extend_quasiFiniteFlat).
Over the interior identify the kernels with the graded pieces of the flag and use the self-duality of the chain for Cartier duality.
acceptance: For g = n = 1 at the cusp with H_2 = μ_p, Gr_1 = ker(Tate(q^p) → Tate(q)) has order p off q = 0 and is trivial on q = 0.
The Cartier divisor D_i attached to Gr_i (Boxer–Pilloni 4.1.8) is owned by HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, which builds it from this target.

hypotheses: n = 1; the interior identification of the normalization with the lattice-chain moduli (normality of that moduli space) is an input owned by ShimuraVarietiesPartII (recorded as a gap).
proofSteps: Given the interior identification, the boundary statement follows from C13/iwahori-normalized-model: by uniqueness of extensions of homomorphisms over the normal base, the extended chain agrees with any extension of the universal chain.
acceptance: For g = 1 the Iwahori lattice-chain moduli is the moduli of p-isogenies E → E′, the Katz–Mazur Γ_0(p) problem, whose compactification is X_0(p) over ℤ_p.
The extended chain restricts on the interior to the universal chain.

nodes.title: Klingen and paramodular level for GSp_4
nodes.statement: Let V = ℤ^4 with basis e_1, …, e_4 and the standard symplectic form of Pilloni §5.1, K = K^pGSp_4(ℤ_p) with K^p neat, and V_1 = pe_1ℤ ⊕ e_2ℤ ⊕ e_3ℤ ⊕ e_4ℤ ⊂ V. The paramodular group scheme is GSp′_4 = GSp(V_1, ⟨·,·⟩) over ℤ, and the arithmetic groups are Γ = GSp_4(ℤ_(p))^+, Γ_par = GSp′_4(ℤ_(p))^+ and Γ_Kli(p) = the automorphisms of (V_1 ⊗ ℤ_(p) → V ⊗ ℤ_(p)) up to positive similitude, a common subgroup of Γ and Γ_par. In moduli terms: Y_K parametrizes abelian surfaces with a prime-to-p polarization; Y_par,K abelian surfaces G′ with a polarization of degree p² (up to ℤ_(p)^×) and K^p-level; Y_Kli(p),K pairs (G, H) with H ⊂ G[p] of order p; and p_1(G, H) = G, p_2(G, H) = (G/H^⊥, λ′), λ′ the descent of p²λ. Over Y_Kli(p) there is the chain G → G/H → G/H^⊥ → G with composite [p].
hypotheses: p any prime; K^p neat. As lattice collections: Y_par is the singleton {V_1}, Y_Kli(p) the collection {V_1 ⊂ V} (C8/pel-lattice-collection).
proofSteps: The groups are stabilizers of the lattices V and V_1 and of the chain V_1 ⊂ V (ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 for the parahoric group schemes).
The moduli descriptions and the maps p_1, p_2 are Pilloni §§6.1.1–6.1.3; the chain uses H^⊥, the orthogonal of H for the Weil pairing on G[p].
acceptance: The chain G → G/H → G/H^⊥ → G has degrees p, p², p with composite [p].
Γ_Kli(p) = Γ ∩ Γ_par.

nodes.title: Klingen and paramodular boundary charts
nodes.statement: For W a totally isotropic direct factor of V (rank 0, 1 or 2) and γ ∈ GSp_4(𝔸_f^p)/K^p, the paramodular and Klingen boundary towers M_{W,γ,·} → B_{W,γ,·} → Y_{W,γ,·} are the normalized boundary towers (C7/normalized-boundary-tower, C8/pel-putative-charts) of the collections of C14/klingen-paramodular-data: M is a torus torsor under T_{W,γ,·}, isogenous to Sym²(V/W^⊥) ⊗ 𝔾_m, over the abelian scheme B (of relative dimension 2 − rank W) over Y_{W,γ,·}, a moduli space of abelian varieties of genus 2 − rank W with K^p-level (and, for Kli(p), a Klingen structure at p depending on the position of W relative to V_1). For the paramodular case M parametrizes 1-motives with a polarization of degree Np² ((N, p) = 1) whose toric character group is V_1/W^⊥. The integral structures X_⋆(T_{W,γ}), X_⋆(T_{W,γ,par}), X_⋆(T_{W,γ,Kli(p)}) are lattices in the cocharacter space Sym²(V/W^⊥)^∨ ⊗ ℚ, and a cone is smooth if its generators s_i extend to a ℤ-basis of the relevant X_⋆(T). A cone decomposition is good if it is projective, satisfies Pilloni's condition 2 on stabilizers, and is smooth for X_⋆(T_{W,γ}) (resp. X_⋆(T_{W,γ,par}), X_⋆(T_{W,γ,Kli(p)})) when it is Γ- (resp. Γ_par-, Γ_Kli(p)-) admissible.
hypotheses: Corrections of sourceIssues E34–E38: the level is K^p-level; the abelian part has genus 2 − rank_ℤ W; B_{W,γ,par} lies over Y_{W,γ,par}; lattices are character or cocharacter groups as stated; condition 3 reads with H = Γ (resp. Γ_par, Γ_Kli(p)).
proofSteps: Specialize C8/pel-putative-charts to the two collections; the toric part of the degenerating 1-motive at W has character group V/W^⊥ (resp. V_1/W^⊥).
Good cone decompositions exist and are cofinal (Faltings–Chai p. 97).
acceptance: For rank W = 2 (the Siegel cusp) the abelian part is trivial and the torus has rank 3.
The paramodular toric character group at W is V_1/W^⊥.

nodes.title: Toroidal compactifications at Klingen and paramodular level (Pilloni, Theorem 6.1.5.1)
nodes.statement: Let Σ be a good cone decomposition that is Γ_Kli(p)- (resp. Γ_par-) admissible. There is a toroidal compactification X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ} of Y_Kli(p)_K (resp. X_{par,K,Σ} of Y_{par,K}) over ℤ_p, the normalized toroidal model of the corresponding lattice collection, with a stratification indexed by Γ_Kli(p)\Σ (resp. Γ_par\Σ) in which the (σ, γ)-stratum is isomorphic to Z_{W,γ,Kli(p),σ} (resp. Z_{W,γ,par,σ}) and the completion along it is that of M_{W,γ,Kli(p),σ} (resp. M_{W,γ,par,σ}) along the stratum; the boundary (the reduced complement of the interior) is a relative Cartier divisor. Their generic fibres are the characteristic-zero toroidal compactifications at the corresponding levels.
hypotheses: Σ good (in particular projective and smooth for the relevant integral structure); strata are listed in the corrected order of sourceIssues E39.
proofSteps: Construct the models by normalization (C8/pel-normalized-toroidal) or as Lan17 normalized blow-ups of the normalized minimal models (C8/normalized-blowup-input); Pilloni's Theorem 6.1.5.1 is the special case of Lan17 Theorem 6.1.
The stratification and completions are C8/pel-strata-completions with the charts of C14/one-motive-charts; the boundary is Cartier by C10/main-theorem.
acceptance: X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ}[1/p] and X_{par,K,Σ}[1/p] are the toroidal compactifications of ShimuraCompactifications C2 at the corresponding levels, base changed to ℚ_p.

sources.match: States existence, stratification and completions of the toroidal compactifications at spherical, Klingen and paramodular level for good cone decompositions, as a special case of Lan's Theorem 6.1, with the paramodular case via Zarhin's trick and normalization.

nodes.title: Klingen and paramodular compactifications are normal and lci
nodes.statement: For Σ good and admissible for the relevant group, X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ} and X_{par,K,Σ} are normal, flat and local complete intersections over ℤ_p. Their non-smooth loci are contained in the non-ordinary locus of the special fibre (ordinary defined pointwise by the p-rank of the p-divisible group, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2), including at the boundary, and have codimension at least 2; the non-smooth locus of the open Y_{par,K} is a finite set of closed points of characteristic p.
hypotheses: Σ good; the interior properties (Y_par,K and Y_Kli(p),K regular, flat and lci over ℤ_p, the non-smooth locus of Y_par,K finite) are Pilloni's Proposition 6.1.4.1, an input owned by ShimuraVarietiesPartII (recorded as a gap).
proofSteps: Normality from the construction by normalization.
The lci property transfers from the interior to the toroidal model for smooth Σ (C8/pel-local-properties).

Non-smooth locus: boundary charts are torus torsors over abelian torsors over modular curves of level away from p (paramodular) or Γ_0(p) (some Klingen cases), smooth over their ordinary loci; combined with the finite non-smooth locus of Y_par this gives codimension ≥ 2 (Pilloni p. 38, corrected: the printed 'codimension 2' holds as 'at least 2', and for Y_par the locus is finite).
acceptance: At the singular point L_0 = ⟨pe_1, e_4⟩ of the paramodular local model the deformation ring is ℤ_p[[X, Y, W, Z]]/(XY − WZ + p), regular and a complete intersection, but not smooth over ℤ_p: its special fibre 𝔽_p[[X, Y, W, Z]]/(XY − WZ) is singular at the origin.

sources.match: States that Y_par and Y_Kli(p) are regular, flat lci with finite non-smooth locus for Y_par, that the toroidal compactifications are normal and lci, and that their non-smooth locus lies in the non-ordinary special fibre and has codimension 2.

nodes.title: The projections from Klingen level
nodes.statement: If Σ is Γ- (resp. Γ_par-) admissible and Σ′ is a Γ_Kli(p)-admissible refinement, then p_1 : Y_Kli(p)_K → Y_K (resp. p_2 : Y_Kli(p)_K → Y_par,K) extends to p_1 : X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ′} → X_{K,Σ} (resp. p_2 : X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ′} → X_{par,K,Σ}). Over X_Kli(p) the interior chain extends to isogenies of semi-abelian schemes G → G′ → G of degrees p³ and p with composite [p], where G is pulled back by p_1 and G′ by p_2. The maps p_1 and p_2 are not finite flat: they are not quasi-finite over the p-rank-zero loci, and not finite flat over the boundary.
hypotheses: Compatible good cone decompositions; the chain G → G′ is the composite G → G/H → G/H^⊥ of the interior.
proofSteps: Extension of p_1, p_2: functoriality of normalized models for subcollections {V} ⊂ {V_1 ⊂ V} and {V_1} ⊂ {V_1 ⊂ V} (C8/pel-functoriality).
The chain extends by extension of homomorphisms over the normal base; degrees and composite are checked on the interior.
Failure of quasi-finiteness over the p-rank-zero locus: fibres of p_1 over a supersingular point contain curves (Pilloni §7.1, footnote 9).
acceptance: Over the ordinary locus the components of X_Kli(p) where G → G′ has étale kernel of rank two and those where it is multiplicative are distinguished by the chain (Pilloni §7.1).

sources.match: Extends the projections from Klingen level to toroidal models for compatible refinements, records the chain G → G′ → G of degrees p³ and p over X_Kli(p), and notes that p_1, p_2 are not finite flat.

nodes.title: The compactified T_{p,2}-correspondence over ℤ_p
nodes.statement: Let C_{p,2} over ℤ_p be the moduli of isogenies p_1^*G → p_2^*G of principally polarized abelian surfaces with K^p-level whose kernel is a totally isotropic (Lagrangian) subgroup of order p² of p_1^*G[p], with the two projections p_1, p_2 to Y_K. For suitable good Σ, Σ′, Σ″ there is a toroidal compactification C_{p,2,Σ″} with p_1 : C_{p,2,Σ″} → X_Σ and p_2 : C_{p,2,Σ″} → X_{Σ′} extending the projections, obtained as the normalized toroidal model of the collection {V, L′} given by the two lattices (Faltings–Chai p. 253). The Hecke operators T_{p,2} and U_{Kli(p),2} built on it are owned by IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, SiegelModularFormsModPn and HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.
hypotheses: Compatible good cone decompositions; the interior moduli of Lagrangian subgroups is an instance of the Siegel parahoric lattice-chain moduli owned by ShimuraVarietiesPartII.
proofSteps: The isogeny with Lagrangian kernel of order p² is the data of a second self-dual-up-to-p lattice; the collection of the two lattices gives a normalized model (C8/pel-normalized-toroidal) with its two projections (C8/pel-functoriality).
Comparison with Faltings–Chai's compactified Hecke correspondences in characteristic zero (ShimuraCompactifications C3, toroidal Hecke correspondences).
acceptance: Over the interior generic fibre p_1 is finite étale of degree (p + 1)(p² + 1).
The generic fibre is the characteristic-zero Hecke correspondence for diag(1, 1, p, p).

nodes.title: Automorphic sheaves of genus two at Klingen and paramodular level
nodes.statement: On X = X_{K,Σ} let ω_G = e^*Ω¹_{G/X} for the semi-abelian G, of rank 2, and Ω^{(k,r)} = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det^r ω_G for (k, r) ∈ ℤ_{≥0} × ℤ, with Ω^{(k,r)}(−D) = Ω^{(k,r)} ⊗ I_D for the boundary D. On X_par define them using G′; on X_Kli(p) use p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)} and p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)}. For a refinement π : X_{Σ′} → X_Σ (of any of the three), π^*Ω^{(k,r)} = Ω^{(k,r)}, Rπ_*O = O and Rπ_*I_{D′} = I_D, so RΓ(Ω^{(k,r)}) and RΓ(Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) do not depend on Σ; only π^*I_D ⊂ I_{D′} holds, with equality only for Σ′ = Σ (sourceIssues E40).
hypotheses: Good cone decompositions; the derived pushforward statements are those of ShimuraCompactifications C3.6–C3.8 for Lan17 models.
proofSteps: Define ω_G by the Hodge bundle of the semi-abelian scheme (ShimuraCompactifications C4.1); pullback compatibility under refinements because G pulls back.
Cohomology independence by the projection formula with Rπ_*O = O and Rπ_*I_{D′} = I_D (ShimuraCompactifications C3.9 in Lan17's setting).
acceptance: RΓ(X_Σ, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is the same for all good Σ.
On X[1/p], Ω^{(k,r)} is the canonical extension of the automorphic bundle of weight (k, r).

nodes.title: Minimal compactifications at Klingen and paramodular level
nodes.statement: X^⋆_par := Proj(⊕_{k≥0} H^0(X_par, ω^k)) and X^⋆_Kli(p) := Proj(⊕_{k≥0} H^0(X_Kli(p), ω^k_J)) are the normalized minimal models of the paramodular and Klingen collections (C8/pel-normalized-minimal, C8/pel-normalized-toroidal), with contractions π_par : X_par → X^⋆_par and π_Kli : X_Kli(p) → X^⋆_Kli(p). The line bundles det ω_G and det ω_{G′} on X_Kli(p) descend to invertible sheaves on X^⋆_Kli(p) (after a fixed positive power) and the map det ω_G → det ω_{G′} induced by G → G′ descends; its non-vanishing locus X^{⋆,≥1}_Kli(p) has preimage the p-rank ≥ 1 locus X^{≥1}_Kli(p). The map X^⋆_Kli(p) → X^⋆ induced by p_1 is proper, and finite over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus X^{⋆,≥1} (p-rank defined pointwise through FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2).
hypotheses: Good Σ; X^⋆ is the good-level minimal compactification (ShimuraCompactifications C5.16); p-rank loci are pointwise.
proofSteps: Construct both minimal models as normalized minimal models and identify them with the Proj by C8/pel-normalized-toroidal (Lan16 Proposition 7.11).

Descent of det ω_G and det ω_{G′}: each is a pullback of an ample line of an auxiliary minimal model (Lan16 Proposition 6.4), so they descend; the map between them descends because it is a section of the descended Hom line, extended over the normal X^⋆_Kli(p) from the complement of codimension ≥ 2.
Finiteness over X^{⋆,≥1}: p_1 is proper and quasi-finite over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus (fibres of the Klingen projection over a point of p-rank ≥ 1 are finite), hence finite (Pilloni p. 101).
acceptance: X^⋆_par is normal, projective and flat over ℤ_p with ample ω.
The map X^⋆_Kli(p) → X^⋆ is finite over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus and not over the supersingular locus.

nodes.title: The GSpin Shimura datum and its Kuga–Satake embedding
nodes.statement: Let (L, Q) be a quadratic ℤ-lattice of signature (n, 2), n ≥ 1, V = L ⊗ ℚ with bilinear form [x, y] = Q(x + y) − Q(x) − Q(y), C(V) its Clifford algebra and G = GSpin(V) ⊂ C^+(V)^× the general spin group, with spinor similitude ν. Let X be the space of oriented negative definite planes in V_ℝ, a G(ℝ)-conjugacy class of homomorphisms h : 𝕊 → G_ℝ. Then (G, X) is a Shimura datum of Hodge type of dimension n with reflex field ℚ, and the action of G on C(V) by left multiplication with a suitable symplectic form ψ_δ(x, y) = tr(x δ y^*) (δ ∈ C^+(V)^× with δ^* = −δ) defines an embedding of Shimura data (G, X) ↪ (GSp(C(V), ψ_δ), S^±) (the Kuga–Satake embedding). If L is self-dual at p, G has a reductive model GSpin(L_{ℤ_(p)}) and the embedding is p-integral after Zarhin's replacement.
hypotheses: Signature (n, 2) with n ≥ 1; for n ≥ 6 the datum is not of PEL type.
proofSteps: GSpin(V) is the subgroup of C^+(V)^× of elements g with g V g^{-1} = V; the spinor similitude is ν(g) = g g^*.
Each oriented negative plane spanned by an oriented orthonormal basis e, f gives h with h(i) = e f; Deligne's axioms hold (MP Introduction, Example; Kisin).
acceptance: For n = 3 and L split the datum is the Siegel datum of genus two.
The Kuga–Satake embedding is p-integral when L is self-dual at p, after Zarhin's replacement.

sources.match: Introduces the GSpin Shimura datum attached to a quadratic space of signature (n, 2) and its Kuga–Satake embedding into a Siegel datum, of Hodge type but not PEL for n ≥ 6.

nodes.title: Cusps of GSpin minimal compactifications
nodes.statement: For the GSpin datum with L self-dual at p and hyperspecial level, the boundary components of 𝒮^BB = 𝒮^min_K (C12/minimal-compactification) are 0- or 1-dimensional: the admissible parabolics are the stabilizers of isotropic lines (zero-dimensional cusps, P with abelian unipotent radical U = W of dimension n) and of isotropic planes I ⊂ L of rank 2 (one-dimensional cusps, U a Heisenberg group with one-dimensional centre W = ∧²I and pure part a modular curve). For a one-dimensional cusp Υ with isotropic plane I set Λ = I^⊥/I, a definite lattice of rank n − 2. The stratification of 𝒮^BB by these cusps is flat over ℤ_(p).
hypotheses: (L, Q) self-dual at p, hyperspecial level; real rank of SO(n, 2) is 2, so isotropic subspaces have dimension ≤ 2.
proofSteps: In characteristic zero, rational boundary components correspond to isotropic subspaces of V (Bruinier–Zemel §§3.2–3.3; Zemel §4): lines give points and planes give modular curves.
Integrally apply C12/minimal-compactification: the strata are quotients of integral models of the boundary pure Shimura varieties, flat over ℤ_(p).
acceptance: For n = 1 (modular or Shimura curves) all cusps are zero-dimensional.
For n ≥ 3 and L isotropic of Witt index 2, both kinds of cusps occur.

sources.match: Records that by Madapusi Pera's Theorem 3 the GSpin integral model has a projective normal minimal compactification with flat stratification whose cusps are zero- or one-dimensional, following Bruinier–Zemel and Zemel.
Describes the boundary components of orthogonal Shimura varieties by isotropic lines and planes (cited by Maulik–Shankar–Tang; not read here).

nodes.title: Fibres over one-dimensional cusps and canonical boundary strata
nodes.statement: Let Υ be a one-dimensional cusp of 𝒮^BB with isotropic plane I and Λ = I^⊥/I. (1) The cone decomposition at Υ is unique (the cone is a ray, W being one-dimensional), so the boundary strata of 𝒮^tor over Υ are canonical. (2) Up to a quotient by a finite group, π^{-1}(Υ) ⊂ 𝒮^tor is a torsor under the abelian scheme ℰ ⊗_ℤ Λ over the modular curve Υ, ℰ the universal elliptic curve. (3) Prime-to-p Hecke correspondences of G(𝔸_f^p) extend uniquely to π^{-1}(𝒮^BB ∖ {zero-dimensional cusps}), with the explicit description on formal completions of C10/functoriality.
hypotheses: Hyperspecial level, L self-dual at p; the finite group in (2) is Δ^fin_K(Φ).
proofSteps: (1): the cone of a one-dimensional cusp lies in the one-dimensional space W(ℝ), so every admissible decomposition restricts to the ray.

(2): in characteristic zero π^{-1}(Υ(ℂ)) is a finite quotient of an ℰ ⊗ Λ-torsor over the modular curve (Zemel Proposition 4.3, Theorem 4.5; Bruinier–Zemel Lemma 3.18, Proposition 3.19); integrally the abelian-scheme torsor of C10/abelian-torsor-extension with A_K(Φ) = ℰ ⊗ Λ.
(3): since the cones over Υ are forced, the compatibility hypothesis of C10/functoriality holds for every Hecke translate on this open part.
acceptance: For n = 2 and L split of signature (2, 2) (products of modular curves), Λ = 0 and π^{-1}(Υ) is finite over the modular curve.

sources.match: Uses the uniqueness of the cone decomposition at one-dimensional cusps to extend Hecke correspondences over the preimage of the complement of the zero-dimensional cusps, and describes π^{-1}(Υ) as a finite quotient of an ℰ ⊗ Λ-torsor over the modular curve, via Madapusi Pera Theorem 4.1.5.
Explicit description of the boundary over one-dimensional cusps of orthogonal Shimura varieties (cited by Maulik–Shankar–Tang; not read here).

nodes.title: Zero-dimensional cusps of GSpin varieties
nodes.statement: At a zero-dimensional cusp attached to an isotropic line ℓ ⊂ L, the unipotent radical U_P is abelian and equal to its centre W ≅ ℓ ⊗ ℓ^⊥/ℓ (of dimension n), the cone H ⊂ W(ℝ) is a component of the positive cone of the Lorentzian space ℓ^⊥/ℓ ⊗ ℝ of signature (n − 1, 1), self-adjoint for the induced form, and the complete local ring of 𝒮^BB_{K_n,k} at the cusp is k[[q^λ]]^{Δ_{K_n}}_{λ≥0} with the action of 𝔹_ℓ of C12/zero-dimensional-cusp-coordinates.
hypotheses: Hyperspecial level; ℓ ≠ p for the 𝔹_ℓ action.
proofSteps: Compute the parabolic stabilizing ℓ: its unipotent radical is the group of Eichler transformations, abelian and isomorphic to ℓ ⊗ ℓ^⊥/ℓ.
The positive cone is that of the Lorentzian space; apply C12/zero-dimensional-cusp-coordinates.
acceptance: For n = 3 (Siegel threefold) the cone at an isotropic line is the cone of positive definite binary quadratic forms, the Siegel cusp.
U_P is abelian of dimension n at a zero-dimensional cusp.

sources.match: Works at a zero-dimensional cusp of the GSpin variety, whose admissible parabolic stabilizes an isotropic line, with lattice B_{K_n} in W(ℚ), the open self-adjoint cone and the invariant power series description of the complete local ring.

gaps.title: Kisin's smoothness of integral models of Hodge type at hyperspecial level
gaps.detail: For a p-integral Hodge embedding (C11/p-integral-embedding) with p > 2 (or p = 2 under Kim–Madapusi Pera), the normalization 𝒮_K of 𝒜_{K‡} ⊗ O_{E,(v)} in Sh_K is smooth over O_{E,(v)}, its complete local rings are quotients of Siegel ones cut out by deformations preserving crystalline tensors, the de Rham tensors s_{α,dR} extend over 𝒮_K with P_dR a G_{ℤ_(p)}-torsor, and 𝒮_K satisfies the extension property for regular formally smooth schemes (Kisin, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 23 (2010), Theorem 2.3.5, Propositions 2.3.8–2.3.9; Madapusi Pera Theorem 4.3.3). gaps.title: Local structure of the Klingen and paramodular moduli over ℤ_p
gaps.detail: Y_par,K and Y_Kli(p),K are regular, flat local complete intersections over ℤ_p, the non-smooth locus of Y_par,K is a finite set of closed points of characteristic p, and these moduli spaces are normal, hence equal to the normalization of the auxiliary models in their generic fibres (Pilloni Proposition 6.1.4.1, from the local models of Yu and of de Jong, with deformation ring ℤ_p[[X, Y, W, Z]]/(XY − WZ + p) at the paramodular singular point). Owner: ShimuraVarietiesPartII (interior models and local models), not yet planned.

gaps.title: Normality of Iwahori and Lagrangian lattice-chain moduli
gaps.detail: For n = 1 the moduli of self-dual chains of p-isogenies of principally polarized abelian schemes (Iwahori level), and the moduli of Lagrangian subgroups of G[p], are normal and flat over ℤ_p, so that they coincide with the interiors of the normalized models (Boxer–Pilloni Remark 4.1.2, interior form; Görtz's flatness of symplectic local models). Owner: ShimuraVarietiesPartII (parahoric lattice-chain moduli), not yet planned.

sourceIssues.printed: The moduli of 1-motives M_{W,γ}, M_{W,γ,Kli(p)}, M_{W,γ,par} are said to carry K_p-level structure; the abelian part is given genus rank_ℤ W; B_{W,γ,par} is placed over Y_{W,γ}.
sourceIssues.correction: Level K^p (away from p); the abelian part has genus 2 − rank_ℤ W; B_{W,γ,par} lies over Y_{W,γ,par}.
sourceIssues.reason: The toric part of the degeneration at W has rank rank_ℤ W, so the abelian part of a genus-two 1-motive has genus 2 − rank W; the level at p is encoded by the lattice, not by a K_p-structure; the diagram on p. 27 already has Y_{W,γ,par}.
sourceIssues.known: Recorded by the paper extraction (PAPER-PILLONI-20/E34, E35, E37); no published correction known.

sourceIssues.printed: The lattices X_⋆(T) are placed in Sym²(V/W^⊥) ⊗ ℚ and smoothness is tested against a lattice of that space; condition 3 is conditioned on H being admissible.
sourceIssues.correction: The lattices in Sym²(V/W^⊥) ⊗ ℚ are character groups X^⋆(T); cones live in X_⋆(T)_ℝ and a cone is smooth if its generators extend to a ℤ-basis of X_⋆(T); condition 3 reads 'if H = Γ (resp. Γ_par, Γ_Kli(p))'.

sourceIssues.known: PAPER-PILLONI-20/E36, E38; no published correction known.

sourceIssues.correction: Rπ_*I_{X_{Σ′}} = I_{X_Σ}; only π^*I_{X_Σ} ⊂ I_{X_{Σ′}} holds, with equality only when Σ′ = Σ.

sourceIssues.printed: Gr_i is treated on all of S^tor as a finite flat group scheme to which Fargues's divisor construction applies.
sourceIssues.correction: Over S^tor, Gr_i is the kernel of an extended isogeny of semi-abelian schemes, quasi-finite and flat but not finite in general at the boundary; it is finite flat over the interior.
sourceIssues.reason: For the Tate curve, ker(Tate(q^p) → Tate(q)) has order p off q = 0 and is trivial at q = 0.
sourceIssues.handling: C13/graded-pieces states the quasi-finite flat statement; the divisor D_i is built by HigherHidaAndColemanTheory from it.
